meta.spec_reference: ISO/IEC 10918-1:1994 / ITU-T Recommendation T.81 (1992), 'Digital Compression and Coding of Continuous-tone Still Images' -- clause B.1.1 marker structure, B.2.2 frame headers (SOF0/1/2/3), B.2.3 scan headers, B.2.4 table definitions (DQT, DHT, DRI, COM), B.2.5 DNL, B.2.6 DHP, annex F baseline Huffman coding, annex G progressive, annex H lossless, annex K the standard tables; ITU-T Recommendation T.87 (1998) JPEG-LS for the SOF-55 (0xFFF7) frame, clause A.1; JFIF Specification Version 1.02 (1 September 1992) for APP0 and the JFXX extensions; Exif 2.2 (JEITA CP-3451) with TIFF 6.0 for the APP1 IFD layout and tag values; Adobe Technical Note #5116 for the APP14 DCT-filter segment; ICC.1:2004-10 / ISO 15076-1 for the APP2 ICC profile blocks; Canon CIFF Specification V1R04 for the APP0 CIFF heap. All of these except ICC.1 are named in the template's own reference list at lines 47-52. The libjpeg/libjpeg-turbo behaviour cited in decoder_gate and in the tier rationales refers to the libjpeg 9 / libjpeg-turbo 2.x error and warning symbols (JERR_NO_SOI, JERR_SOS_NO_SOF, JERR_SOF_DUPLICATE, JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED, JERR_BAD_PRECISION, JERR_BAD_SAMPLING, JERR_BAD_J_COLORSPACE, JERR_BAD_COMPONENT_ID, JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION, JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE, JERR_NO_QUANT_TABLE, JERR_DQT_INDEX, JERR_BAD_HUFF_TABLE, JWRN_HUFF_BAD_CODE, JWRN_HUFF_BAD_INDEX, JWRN_MUST_RESYNC, JWRN_HIT_MARKER, JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA).

schema_extensions.name: also_declared_at
schema_extensions.why: Several field names are declared more than once inside the same struct because the template redeclares them in different switch branches (APP0.App0Type at lines 1105 and 1120, APP0.xThumbnail at 1111/1130/1138, DIRENTRY.tagNumber at 766/769/772, QuanTable.qTable at 1444/1446, APP12.count at 1289/1293, APP13.padding at 1346/1351). The base schema's single evidence line would lose all but the first declaration, and a constraints key can only appear once, so the extra declaration sites are recorded as {line, snippet} pairs.

schema_extensions.name: extra_evidence
schema_extensions.why: JPEG constraints are rarely evidenced by the declaration line alone: the value of a marker field is proven by its switch case and its enum constant, a length field's arithmetic by the array it bounds, a lookahead by its call site. extra_evidence is an array of additional {line, snippet} pairs, each verbatim, so every claim in an entry stays grounded in a real line.

schema_extensions.name: excluded_values
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries (Tier B and Tier C)
schema_extensions.why: Some fields are free across their whole width except for one or two individual values the specification forbids (SOFx.X_image and SOFx.Y_image may not be 0; SOS.Ah and SOS.Al may not be 14 or 15; APP0.Xdensity and Ydensity may not be 0; CifDirEntry.data_type may not be 7; DIRENTRY.dataFormat may not be 0). Naming single illegal values is not a span narrowing of any kind and no key of that forbidden shape is used, so this needs its own key.

schema_extensions.name: derives_from_length
schema_extensions.where: constraints entries (Tier C and Tier A/B)
schema_extensions.why: Names the field that fixes this field's byte extent when the value itself is free (APP13.data is sized by APP13.size, COMMENT.comment by COMMENT.szSection). It keeps 'the bytes are free' separate from 'the count is computed', which the base schema has no slot for.

schema_extensions.name: value_count
schema_extensions.why: Records a fixed array cardinality that belongs to the type rather than to a value (QuanTable.qTable has 64 elements, Huffmann_Table.length has 16, HTV has sum(L1..L16)). It counts elements; it narrows no element's value.

schema_extensions.name: evidence
schema_extensions.why: Document-level rules in this template are grounded in specific lines (the dispatch switch, the FindFirst call, the fill-byte loop), so structure rules carry the same {line, snippet} evidence shape as constraints entries.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead
schema_extensions.why: The template's marker dispatch reads into a local (local WORD NextMarker at line 1536) and switches on it at line 1545, so there is no field to hang the per-call-site value set on. The base schema forbids entries for locals, so the ReadUShort value set is recorded on the ordering rule instead, together with the 0xFFFF fill-byte lookahead at line 1542.

schema_extensions.name: fill_bytes
schema_extensions.why: JPEG tolerates any number of 0xFF fill bytes before a marker (template line 1542). That is neither forbidden data nor a cardinality limit, so it needs its own rule name.

schema_extensions.name: then-extension keys
schema_extensions.why: The base 'then' shape covers a field plus a value set. JPEG's conditional rules also need: fields (a list, for the four SOS parameters that move together), tier and type (a dependency may promote a free field to a computed one), required_values (per-field fixed values), algorithm, pattern, rule, detail and condition (the textual form of the relation), codec (for a conditional payload such as the nested EXIF thumbnail), required, cardinality and value_count. All are additions inside 'then'; none renames or drops a base key.

schema_extensions.name: not_in
schema_extensions.why: Several template branches are the else case of an identifier test (an APP0 that is neither JFIF nor JFXX, an APP13 block signature that is none of the four). Expressing that needs negated membership, which the base when-operators do not include.

schema_extensions.name: name
schema_extensions.why: A short human-readable label for each axis, used in the report and in meta.axis_coverage; 'field' stays the authoritative key.

schema_extensions.name: tier
schema_extensions.why: Records the tier of the field the axis covers, so a reader can tell at a glance whether the axis protects a free field (Tier C) or insists on the full legal set of an enumerated one (Tier B).

schema_extensions.name: must_emit_full_legal_set
schema_extensions.why: For Tier A and Tier B axes the instruction cannot be 'leave it unconstrained'; it is 'emit every legal value, including the awkward ones'. This key carries that instruction and complements must_remain_unconstrained.

schema_extensions.name: also_covers
schema_extensions.why: Several fields vary together as one semantic unit (the two JFIF thumbnail dimensions, the pair of density words, the seven CIFF image-spec words, the eight EXIF tag enumerations, the six Flash bitfields). They are listed on the axis of the field that leads the group, so every Tier C field is axis-covered without inventing grouped axes.

schema_extensions.name: how_varied
schema_extensions.why: Sampling instruction for the generator: how to vary the field so the population actually spans it (uniform, per-file choice, edge-biased, all-values rotation).

schema_extensions.name: diversity_budget
schema_extensions.why: For the few axes whose span controls output size (the JFIF thumbnail dimensions, the EXIF and CIFF entry counts), this states which structure output_budget the bytes land in. It never caps a value; it only routes the bytes to a budget.

schema_extensions.name: notes
schema_extensions.why: Carries anything else a rewrite step needs about an axis, notably the pairing instruction 'derive the payload from this field' where interacts_with alone would be ambiguous.

schema_extensions.name: axis_coverage
schema_extensions.why: Provenance block: how many constraints entries are named directly by a diversity axis, how many more are covered through also_covers, and the explicit list of entries no axis names with the reason for each, so the coverage claim is checkable.

meta.structure_note: A JPEG file is a big-endian sequence of 0xFF-prefixed marker segments, each length-prefixed by a 16-bit count except the standalone markers (SOI, EOI, RST0..RST7, TEM): SOI opens the file, then table-definition (DQT, DHT, DRI), application (APP0..APP15) and comment (COM) segments in any order, then exactly one frame header (SOF0/1/2/3, or SOF55 for JPEG-LS) that fixes the geometry and the components, then one or more scan headers (SOS) each followed by an entropy-coded segment that runs unbroken to the next marker, and finally EOI. This format does have a compressed payload and it is the whole point of the file: JPGFILE.scanData must be a genuine Huffman-coded JPEG scan with 0xFF byte stuffing and the MCU count the frame geometry implies (see its payload_wellformedness entry), and two further opaque arrays must hold real structures -- APP2.data a reassemblable ICC profile, and APP1.imageData a complete nested JPEG when the EXIF Compression tag is 6. Everything else in the file is metadata that libjpeg skips or stores without interpreting.

CifDirEntry.storage_method.tier_rationale: Tier B: a finite selector whose reserved codings still change which branch of the entry layout is read, so all four two-bit values are recorded and none dropped.
CifDirEntry.storage_method.description: Two-bit CIFF storage selector: whether the record's value lives in the heap area at oData (0) or inline in the 8-byte entry (1).

evidence.snippet: uint16 storage_method : 2; // 00 in heap, 01 in entry

CifDirEntry.storage_method.notes: Underlying enum CIFFTagStg (lines 592-597); values 2 and 3 are named kStg_reversed2/kStg_reversed3 in the template, i.e. reserved by the CIFF specification but still representable in two bits. The template compares this field against kStg_InHeapSpace at lines 576 and 682.

CifDirEntry.data_type.tier_rationale: Tier B: a three-bit selector with seven defined meanings, each selecting a different value-parsing branch, so every defined value is recorded.
CifDirEntry.data_type.description: Three-bit CIFF data-type selector; shifted left by 11 and OR-ed with id_code it forms the full CIFF tag type the template switches on.
CifDirEntry.data_type.notes: Underlying enum CIFFTagDataType (lines 599-607) lists the seven defined types as 0x0000/0x0800/0x1000/0x1800/0x2000/0x2800/0x3000, i.e. data_type 0..6. The template switches on data_type << 11 | id_code at lines 580 and 687 and on data_type << 11 at line 700. Value 7 is representable in three bits but is defined by no CIFF tag type, so it is excluded rather than enumerated.

CifDirEntry.id_code.tier_rationale: Tier B: a finite tag vocabulary, but id_code alone is ambiguous because the same 11-bit id appears under several data_type values, so the recognised ids are listed and the data_type pairing is carried in dependencies.
CifDirEntry.id_code.description: Eleven-bit CIFF tag id; combined with data_type it names the record (kTC_ImageFormat, kTC_ImageSpec, kTC_CameraObject and the rest of the CIFFTagType vocabulary).
CifDirEntry.id_code.notes: Partial because enum CIFFTagType (lines 609-644) defines the ids only in combination with a data_type prefix: the values listed are the low 11 bits of every kTC_* constant in that enum, with duplicates from different prefixes collapsed (e.g. kTC_Description 0x0805 and kTC_TargetImageType 0x100a both contribute id 0x0005 and 0x000a). Camera-specific CIFF tags outside this enum are parsed by the template's default branch as eight raw bytes. The only ids that change the template's control flow are kTC_ImageFormat (0x1803 -> inline fileFormat + targetCompressionRatio at lines 581-584) and kTC_ImageSpec (0x1810 -> a DC_IMAGESPEC record at lines 688-698).

CifDirEntry.sData.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is an offset/size the parser dereferences to find the record's value; a wrong value makes it read the value block from the wrong place, so this record and every record after it in the directory are mis-parsed.
CifDirEntry.sData.description: CIFF heap value size in bytes: the number of bytes stored at oData inside the CIFF heap.
CifDirEntry.sData.algorithm: byte count of the value block the entry points into the heap for; the template uses it directly as an array extent (byte bData[sData] at line 703, char sData[sData] at line 708) and shifts it for wider element types (sData>>1 at line 713, sData>>2 at lines 718-719)
CifDirEntry.sData.covers: the heap value block at CIFF-heap-relative offset oData
CifDirEntry.sData.notes: Byte order follows APP0.ByteOrder ('II' selects LittleEndian() at line 1156). The same word is reused as cDirSize for a nested directory at line 725.

CifDirEntry.oData.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is an offset/size the parser dereferences to find the record's value; a wrong value makes it read the value block from the wrong place, so this record and every record after it in the directory are mis-parsed.
CifDirEntry.oData.description: CIFF heap value offset: bytes from the start of the CIFF heap to the entry's value block.
CifDirEntry.oData.algorithm: byte offset from the CIFF heap base; the template seeks to myOffset + oData at line 684, where myOffset is the directory block's own offset (line 670)
CifDirEntry.oData.covers: position of the heap value block, not a byte count
CifDirEntry.oData.notes: Must land inside the CIFF heap carried by this APP0 segment; 0 means the very start of that heap.

CifDirEntry.fileFormat.tier_rationale: Tier C: no JPEG decoder inspects Canon CIFF metadata and this template only stores the word, so pinning it would remove file-level diversity without reaching any new code.
CifDirEntry.fileFormat.description: CIFF kTC_ImageFormat record's file-format word, read inline when storage_method is kStg_InRecordEntry and the tag type is kTC_ImageFormat (0x1803).
CifDirEntry.fileFormat.notes: CIFF V1R04 (cited at template line 50) defines bit fields inside this word, but the template reads it as a plain uint32 and never compares it, so nothing here is a decoder gate.

CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.tier_rationale: Tier C: an unvalidated float in camera-private metadata; every one of its 2^32 bit patterns parses identically, so constraining it would only cost diversity.
CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.description: CIFF kTC_ImageFormat record's target compression ratio, an IEEE-754 single stored inline next to fileFormat.
CifDirEntry.targetCompressionRatio.notes: A float whose bit pattern is free, including NaN and infinity: the template stores it and makes no comparison.

CDIR.nDirEntry.tier_rationale: Tier C: a repeat count, and the one field that decides how much of the CIFF directory the parser walks. Capping it would collapse every CIFF-bearing file to the same shape for no depth at all, since no image decoder validates the count.
CDIR.nDirEntry.description: Number of CifDirEntry records that follow in this CIFF directory block; the template allocates and loops over exactly this many entries.
CDIR.nDirEntry.notes: The count is read at the offset stored in the last four bytes of the directory block (local DWORD S = ReadInt(myOffset + cDirSize - 4) at line 671, then FSeek to cDirOffset + S at line 672), so the entries are not necessarily immediately after the block start. Total CIFF bytes stay bounded by APP0.szSection, which is the segment's own length field.

CDIR.szValues.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template reads this word back and compares it against the value it fetched from the last four bytes of the directory block; a mismatch means the directory block is laid out differently from what the offsets claim, so the entries and their heap values desynchronise.
CDIR.szValues.description: Trailing DWORD of the CIFF directory block: the offset of the entry array inside the block, repeated here so the block is self-describing.
CDIR.szValues.algorithm: must equal the DWORD stored at cDirOffset + cDirSize - 4, which the template reads into local S at line 671 and seeks to at line 672; the field's own comment states the equality
CDIR.szValues.covers: the four bytes at the end of the CIFF directory block
CDIR.szValues.notes: cDirSize itself is derived: cDirSize = szSection - 2 - HeaderLength (line 1163), so this value is ultimately a function of APP0.szSection and APP0.HeaderLength.

DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension recorded in camera-private CIFF metadata. The image that actually gets decoded is described by SOFx.X_image/Y_image, so pinning this word would remove diversity without changing what any decoder does.
DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.description: CIFF kTC_ImageSpec record's declared image width in pixels.
DC_IMAGESPEC.imageWidth.notes: Not the frame width the JPEG decoder uses; it is metadata only.

DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension recorded in camera-private CIFF metadata. The image that actually gets decoded is described by SOFx.X_image/Y_image, so pinning this word would remove diversity without changing what any decoder does.
DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.description: CIFF kTC_ImageSpec record's declared image height in pixels.
DC_IMAGESPEC.imageHeight.notes: Not the frame height the JPEG decoder uses; it is metadata only.

DC_IMAGESPEC.pixelAspectRatio.tier_rationale: Tier C: an unvalidated float in metadata; every bit pattern parses the same way, so constraining it can only cost diversity.
DC_IMAGESPEC.pixelAspectRatio.description: CIFF kTC_ImageSpec pixel aspect ratio, an IEEE-754 single.

DC_IMAGESPEC.rotationAngle.tier_rationale: Tier C: a signed metadata integer no decoder validates; leaving it free costs nothing and keeps negative and large values in the generated population.
DC_IMAGESPEC.rotationAngle.description: CIFF kTC_ImageSpec rotation angle, a signed 32-bit integer.

DC_IMAGESPEC.componentBitDepth.tier_rationale: Tier C: a bit depth a careful reader would want to pin to 8, but the JPEG decoder takes its sample precision from SOFx.precision and never reads this word, so pinning it would cost diversity and buy no depth.

DC_IMAGESPEC.colorBitDepth.tier_rationale: Tier C: same reasoning as componentBitDepth -- the decoder's bit depth comes from SOFx.precision, not from this metadata word.

DC_IMAGESPEC.colorBW.tier_rationale: Tier C: a metadata flag no decoder validates; the decoder learns the colour layout from SOFx.nr_comp and the sampling factors instead, so this word stays free.

DIRENTRY.tagNumber.tier_rationale: Tier B: a finite tag vocabulary in which each recognised tag sends the template down a different value-parsing or nested-directory branch, so every tag that changes control flow is recorded.
DIRENTRY.tagNumber.description: EXIF/TIFF tag id of this directory entry; which vocabulary applies is decided by the IFD_dirtype pushed onto the template's stack before the enclosing IFD is parsed.
DIRENTRY.tagNumber.notes: Partial on purpose, with the reason stated here as the schema requires: the three underlying enums are enormous (typedef enum tagExifTag / ExifTag spans lines 169-496 with roughly 300 constants, enum <WORD> GeoTag spans lines 498-530, typedef enum tagCasioTag2 / CasioTag2 spans lines 534-563), and the great majority of them are inert -- they are read by the template's default branch as raw bytes and are never looked at by a JPEG decoder, which does not parse APP1 at all. The values listed are exactly those the template switches on: Make/Model at lines 944-951, the nested-IFD tags ExifOffset/GPSInfo/InteropOffset at lines 1033-1050, MakerNote at line 1051, CasioPreviewThumbnail at line 1063, the thumbnail geometry tags Compression/ThumbnailOffset/ThumbnailLength/StripOffsets/StripByteCounts at lines 1203-1213, and the eight tags that get an inline enum interpretation at lines 788-874. The declared type alternates with the IFD kind: ExifTag (line 766) for an EXIF or Interop IFD, GeoTag (line 769) for the GPS IFD, CasioTag2 (line 772) for a Casio MakerNote IFD, selected through enum IFD_dirtype (lines 73-77) and the Stack_push/Stack_pop helpers. Any tag id at all is accepted; unrecognised ids are not an error.

DIRENTRY.dataFormat.tier_rationale: Tier B: a twelve-value enum whose members select twelve different value-parsing branches; narrowing it would delete branches for no depth, because the template tolerates any code and merely skips the entry when it is out of range.
DIRENTRY.dataFormat.description: EXIF data-type code: the element type of this entry's value, used with nComponent to compute the value's byte length through dataFormatLength[].
DIRENTRY.dataFormat.notes: Underlying typedef enum tagDataFormat / DataFormat at lines 746-759; the element sizes are const local int dataFormatLength[13] = {0,1,1,2,4,8,1,1,2,4,8,4,8} at line 744. The template tests 1 <= dataFormat && dataFormat < 13 at lines 780, 786 and 955, so 0 and 13..65535 are representable but out of range: they make the entry be skipped (continue at line 956) rather than rejected. Value 0 is therefore excluded here rather than enumerated, since it names no data type.

DIRENTRY.nComponent.tier_rationale: Tier C: a count that sizes every value array in the entry. It is the field a size-conscious author would cap first, and capping it would make every EXIF block in the population identical for no depth -- libjpeg never parses APP1, so no gate is bought.
DIRENTRY.nComponent.description: Number of value elements of type dataFormat in this EXIF entry; multiplied by dataFormatLength[dataFormat] it gives the value's byte length.
DIRENTRY.nComponent.notes: The template's own arithmetic is the constraint that matters, and it is recorded as a dependency rather than as a bound here: length = dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent (line 781); if length <= 4 the value is stored inline followed by padding to four bytes (lines 786, 921-922), otherwise the entry holds offsetData instead (line 924). Total EXIF bytes stay inside APP1.szSection.

DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive nine-member enum declared in the template; each member is a distinct branch of a metadata reader's lookup table, so none is dropped.
DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.description: EXIF tag 0x8822 value, reinterpreted as a named enum when the entry's value is four bytes or fewer.
DIRENTRY.ExposureProgram.notes: Declared as an anonymous enum <short> at lines 789-799 and reached only when tagNumber == ExposureProgram (0x8822, line 788) and the value fits inline (line 786). EXIF 2.2 defines 0..8 exactly as listed.

DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive enum declared in the template including the awkward 255 = MM_other member; dropping it would delete a lookup branch for nothing.
DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.description: EXIF tag 0x9207 value, reinterpreted as a named enum.
DIRENTRY.MeteringMode.notes: Declared at lines 802-811; MM_other is explicitly assigned 255 at line 810, so the legal set is 0..6 plus 255 and nothing in between.

DIRENTRY.LightSource.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive enum declared in the template; the gaps (5..8 and 24..254) are not legal values because LS_Fine_weather is assigned 9 explicitly at line 820, so the enumerated set really is the whole legal set.
DIRENTRY.LightSource.description: EXIF tag 0x9208 value, reinterpreted as a named enum of illumination conditions.
DIRENTRY.LightSource.notes: Declared at lines 814-836; LS_other_light_scoure is assigned 255 at line 835.

DIRENTRY.unused.tier_rationale: Tier C: reserved bits nobody checks. A metadata reader that decodes the Flash tag masks off the seven bits it understands, so leaving these free adds entropy to every EXIF block without costing any parse depth.
DIRENTRY.unused.description: Nine high bits of the EXIF Flash tag (0x9209) that EXIF 2.2 reserves; the template reads them into a field it names 'unused'.
DIRENTRY.unused.notes: BitfieldLeftToRight() is set at lines 56-57, so with the big-endian EXIF word the declaration order is the bit order: unused occupies bits 15..7, red_eye_mode bit 6, flash_function bit 5, flash_mode bits 4..3, flash_return bits 2..1 and flash_fired bit 0 -- exactly the EXIF 2.2 Flash layout.

DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.tier_rationale: Tier B: a one-bit flag with both values legal and both distinct branches in a metadata reader, so both are recorded.
DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.description: EXIF Flash tag bit 6: red-eye reduction mode did not fire (0) or fired (1).
DIRENTRY.red_eye_mode.notes: Declared inside the Flash tag bitfield group at lines 839-844.

DIRENTRY.flash_function.tier_rationale: Tier B: a one-bit flag; both values are legal and both are read.
DIRENTRY.flash_function.description: EXIF Flash tag bit 5: 1 means no flash function (the flash cannot fire).
DIRENTRY.flash_function.notes: Declared inside the Flash tag bitfield group at lines 839-844.

DIRENTRY.flash_mode.tier_rationale: Tier B: a two-bit field whose four codings are all defined by EXIF 2.2, so all four are recorded.
DIRENTRY.flash_mode.description: EXIF Flash tag bits 4..3: 0 = unknown, 1 = compulsory flash firing, 2 = compulsory flash suppression, 3 = auto mode.
DIRENTRY.flash_mode.notes: Declared inside the Flash tag bitfield group at lines 839-844.

DIRENTRY.flash_return.tier_rationale: Tier B: a two-bit field; the reserved coding 1 is included because it is representable and a reader still branches on it.
DIRENTRY.flash_return.description: EXIF Flash tag bits 2..1: 0 = no return-light detection function, 1 = reserved, 2 = return light detected, 3 = return light not detected.
DIRENTRY.flash_return.notes: Declared inside the Flash tag bitfield group at lines 839-844.

DIRENTRY.flash_fired.tier_rationale: Tier B: a one-bit flag; both values are legal and both are read.
DIRENTRY.flash_fired.description: EXIF Flash tag bit 0: 0 = flash did not fire, 1 = flash fired.
DIRENTRY.flash_fired.notes: Declared inside the Flash tag bitfield group at lines 839-844.

DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive three-member enum declared in the template.
DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.description: EXIF tag 0xa402 value, reinterpreted as a named enum.
DIRENTRY.ExposureMode.notes: Declared at lines 847-851, reached only when tagNumber == ExposureMode (line 846).

DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive two-member enum declared in the template.
DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.description: EXIF tag 0xa403 value, reinterpreted as a named enum.
DIRENTRY.WhiteBalance.notes: Declared at lines 854-857, reached only when tagNumber == WhiteBalance (line 853).

DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive four-member enum declared in the template.
DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.description: EXIF tag 0xa406 value, reinterpreted as a named enum.
DIRENTRY.SceneCaptureType.notes: Declared at lines 860-865, reached only when tagNumber == SceneCaptureType (line 859).

DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive four-member enum declared in the template.
DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.description: EXIF tag 0xa40c value, reinterpreted as a named enum.
DIRENTRY.SubjectDistanceRange.notes: Declared at lines 868-873, reached only when tagNumber == SubjectDistanceRange (line 867).

DIRENTRY.usValue.tier_rationale: Tier C: a general-purpose value slot whose meaning is decided by the tag, so pinning the slot would forbid most tags' values and destroy EXIF diversity. Where a tag does define a legal set, the dependency section narrows it -- that is a format rule, not an arbitrary cap.
DIRENTRY.usValue.description: Inline uShort value element of an EXIF entry whose dataFormat is uShort; the template reads nComponent of these in a loop.
DIRENTRY.usValue.notes: The one tag that turns this slot into an enumeration is Compression (0x0103): the template copies usValue into local compression at line 1204 and compares it against 6 at line 1219 to decide whether the EXIF thumbnail is a nested JPEG. That comparison is carried as a dependency.

DIRENTRY.ulValue.tier_rationale: Tier C: the same four bytes are a plain value for most tags and a pointer for a handful of others, so the field itself stays free and the pointer cases are expressed as dependencies.
DIRENTRY.ulValue.description: Inline uLong (uint32) value element of an EXIF entry whose dataFormat is uLong1; for the offset-bearing tags it holds a TIFF-header-relative offset instead of a plain number.
DIRENTRY.ulValue.notes: The template dereferences this slot as an offset for ExifOffset (line 1034), GPSInfo (line 1040), InteropOffset (line 1046), MakerNote (line 1054) and CasioPreviewThumbnail (line 1064), and copies it into thumbOffset at lines 1206-1208 for ThumbnailOffset/StripOffsets. All of those offsets are relative to the TIFF header captured in local offset at line 1180.

DIRENTRY.padding.tier_rationale: Tier C: padding whose value is unchecked. TIFF requires the bytes to be present but says nothing about their contents, so they are free entropy.
DIRENTRY.padding.description: Fill bytes that pad an inline EXIF value up to four bytes; the count is 4 - length where length = dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent.
DIRENTRY.padding.notes: The extent, not the value, is the rule: the template emits uchar padding[4 - length] only when length != 4 (lines 921-922). That extent is recorded as a dependency.

DIRENTRY.offsetData.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the pointer half of a 12-byte EXIF entry; the template seeks to offset + offsetData to read the value, so a wrong value makes it read the entry's data from the wrong place and the whole EXIF block desynchronises.
DIRENTRY.offsetData.description: Offset in bytes from the start of the TIFF header to this entry's value, present only when the value is longer than four bytes.
DIRENTRY.offsetData.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header (local offset, captured at line 1180) to the value block; the value block is dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent bytes long and must lie inside the APP1 segment
DIRENTRY.offsetData.covers: position of the out-of-line value, not a byte count
DIRENTRY.offsetData.notes: Mutually exclusive with the inline value plus padding: the template takes the inline branch when 1 <= dataFormat < 13 and 0 <= length <= 4 (line 786) and the offsetData branch otherwise (lines 923-925). Byte order follows APP1.align.

IFD.nDirEntry.tier_rationale: Tier C: the repeat count that decides how much EXIF metadata a file carries. Capping it would make every generated EXIF block the same size and shape, and no JPEG decoder reads APP1 at all, so nothing would be gained.
IFD.nDirEntry.description: Number of 12-byte DIRENTRY records in this image file directory; the template allocates and loops over exactly this many.
IFD.nDirEntry.notes: Total EXIF bytes stay inside APP1.szSection, which is the segment's length field and is therefore the real size control. The template also honours nextIFDoffset to walk a chain of IFDs (lines 1191-1196).

IFD.nextIFDoffset.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template treats a nonzero value as a pointer and seeks to offset + nextIFDoffset to parse the thumbnail IFD; a wrong value sends the IFD parse into arbitrary file bytes, so all the metadata that follows is mis-parsed.
IFD.nextIFDoffset.description: Offset in bytes from the TIFF header to the next image file directory, or 0 when this is the last one.
IFD.nextIFDoffset.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header (local offset at line 1180) to the next IFD's nDirEntry word; 0 terminates the chain. The template tests it for nonzero at line 1191 and seeks to offset + nextIFDoffset at line 1192
IFD.nextIFDoffset.covers: position of the next IFD, not a byte count
IFD.nextIFDoffset.notes: Exif 2.2 allows exactly one thumbnail IFD after the main image IFD, so the chain is main IFD -> thumbnail IFD -> 0. Byte order follows APP1.align.

IFD.Header.tier_rationale: Tier C: the template reads the six bytes unconditionally and never compares them, and no JPEG decoder looks inside a MakerNote, so pinning them would remove entropy and buy no depth.
IFD.Header.description: Six-byte header the template reads at the start of a Casio QV-R62 MakerNote, immediately before the Casio IFD that follows it.
IFD.Header.notes: Reached only for a Casio QV-R62 file: the MakerNote branch first requires CameraMake == 'CASIO COMPUTER CO.,LTD' and CameraModel == 'QV-R62' (lines 1052-1053), and those two buffers are filled from the Make and Model EXIF tags at lines 945 and 949. exiftool documents this MakerNote header as the ASCII string 'QVC\0\0\0', but because neither the template nor a JPEG decoder checks it, the value is left free.

APP0.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
APP0.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian APP0 marker (0xFFE0) that opens the JFIF/JFXX/CIFF application segment; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1569.
APP0.marker.notes: M_APP0 = 0xFFE0 is defined in enum tagID at line 143 with the comment 'Jfif marker'. JFIF 1.02 requires this segment to be the first one after SOI when the file claims to be JFIF.

APP0.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
APP0.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
APP0.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; the payload length depends on which APP0 flavour the identifier selects, and the template derives every inner extent from this field (szSection - 8 at lines 1125, 1135, 1146; szSection - 2 at lines 1163, 1166, 1170)
APP0.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the whole APP0 payload: the identifier, and then either the JFIF main fields (14 bytes plus 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail thumbnail bytes), or the JFXX extension body (szSection - 8 bytes after extension_code), or the Canon CIFF header and heap (szSection - 2 bytes), or szSection - 2 unknown bytes
APP0.szSection.notes: Maximum 65535 because the field is a WORD, so an APP0 payload can hold at most 65533 bytes.

APP0.App0Type.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP0.App0Type.description: Five-byte identifier at the start of the APP0 payload that says which application format the segment carries; 'JFIF\0' selects the JFIF main segment parsed at lines 1105-1117.
APP0.App0Type.notes: The lookahead is made through the template's own helper ReadStringN(pos, n) (defined at lines 96-101, which calls ReadBytes), compared against the literal "JFIF\0" at line 1103. The same field name is declared again at line 1120 for the JFXX flavour, where the compared literal is "JFXX\0" (line 1118); the JFXX case is carried as a dependency rather than as a second value here, because the two flavours have completely different payloads. A third APP0 flavour, Canon CIFF, is selected by a two-byte "II"/"MM" plus "HEAPJPGM" lookahead at lines 1148-1149 and never uses this field at all. Pinned Tier A because it is the segment's magic identifier: JFIF 1.02 clause 3.1 requires exactly these five bytes, and it is the byte string that makes both this template and a JFIF-aware reader enter the JFIF branch at all.

APP0.versionHigh.tier_rationale: Tier B: JFIF defines only two major versions, 1 and 2, and each selects a different segment layout, so both are recorded and neither is dropped.
APP0.versionHigh.description: JFIF major version number, one byte, read as an 8-bit bitfield of a short.
APP0.versionHigh.notes: JFIF 1.02 is version 1.02; JFIF 2.00 (version 2) replaces the extension block with an extension-code byte and a different trailer, which this template does not model, so a generator that emits major version 2 must still keep szSection consistent with the bytes it writes. libjpeg stores the version without validating it, so a wrong value does not abort the decode -- it is therefore not Tier A.

APP0.versionLow.tier_rationale: Tier B: JFIF defines minor versions 00, 01 and 02, so all three are recorded.
APP0.versionLow.description: JFIF minor version number, one byte.
APP0.versionLow.notes: Paired with versionHigh: 1.00, 1.01 and 1.02 are the released JFIF 1.x revisions (the template header cites jfif3.pdf at line 48). Minor version does not change the segment layout, so it is a free choice among the three legal values.

APP0.units.tier_rationale: Tier B: a three-value enum defined by JFIF 1.02 clause 3.1; each value changes how a reader interprets the two density words that follow, so all three are recorded.
APP0.units.description: JFIF density units: 0 = no units (Xdensity/Ydensity are then a pixel aspect ratio), 1 = dots per inch, 2 = dots per centimetre.
APP0.units.notes: libjpeg copies this byte into cinfo->density_unit without validating it, so the value never gates the decode -- it is Tier B, not Tier A, and none of the three values should be dropped.

APP0.Xdensity.tier_rationale: Tier C: a free 16-bit metadata word. libjpeg stores it and never branches on it, so pinning it would make every JFIF block in the population identical for no depth at all.
APP0.Xdensity.description: JFIF horizontal density, or the horizontal part of the pixel aspect ratio when units is 0.
APP0.Xdensity.notes: excluded_values carries the single value JFIF 1.02 forbids ('the value shall not be zero') rather than any span narrowing: every other WORD is legal and must stay reachable. libjpeg does not enforce this, so a generator may treat the exclusion as advisory.

APP0.Ydensity.tier_rationale: Tier C: same reasoning as Xdensity -- an unvalidated metadata word that only adds diversity, so it stays completely free.
APP0.Ydensity.description: JFIF vertical density, or the vertical part of the pixel aspect ratio when units is 0.
APP0.Ydensity.notes: excluded_values carries the single value JFIF 1.02 forbids rather than any span narrowing. With units == 0 the pair (Xdensity, Ydensity) is a pixel aspect ratio, and JFIF recommends 1:1, which is one point in a free two-dimensional space, not a constraint on it.

APP0.xThumbnail.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It is exactly the kind of field that must not be pinned to a small set -- the thumbnail extent is 3*xThumbnail*yThumbnail bytes and the parser derives it, so the correct move is to derive the thumbnail from these two bytes and leave them free.
APP0.xThumbnail.description: JFIF thumbnail width in pixels; together with yThumbnail it sizes the 3-byte-per-pixel RGB thumbnail array that follows.
APP0.xThumbnail.notes: The template reads the thumbnail only when both dimensions are nonzero (line 1113) and allocates rgb[(ushort)xThumbnail * yThumbnail] (line 1116); the (ushort) cast is the template's own guard against the 8-bit multiply overflowing. The same field name is redeclared for the JFXX palette (line 1130) and RGB (line 1138) thumbnails, where it sizes pixel[] instead. Total APP0 bytes stay inside APP0.szSection, which is the size control.

APP0.yThumbnail.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension, free for the same reason as xThumbnail -- capping it would collapse the thumbnail space without buying a single extra decoder branch.
APP0.yThumbnail.description: JFIF thumbnail height in pixels; the other factor of the thumbnail array extent.
APP0.yThumbnail.notes: Both dimensions must be zero or both nonzero for the template to read a thumbnail (line 1113); the pairing is recorded as a dependency. Redeclared for the JFXX flavours at lines 1131 and 1139.

APP0.extension_code.tier_rationale: Tier B: a three-value enum that the template switches on, each value producing a completely different payload layout, so all three are recorded and none dropped.
APP0.extension_code.description: JFXX extension code selecting the thumbnail encoding: 0x10 = a complete nested JPEG, 0x11 = a 256-colour palette plus indexed pixels, 0x13 = 24-bit RGB triplets.
APP0.extension_code.notes: The three switch cases are at lines 1123, 1129 and 1137. Any other byte reaches the default branch, which reads the remaining szSection - 8 bytes as unknown (line 1146) -- tolerated by the parser but defined by no JFIF document, so it is not enumerated here. 0x10 makes the payload a nested JPGFILE bounded by szSection - 8 (lines 1124-1127).

APP0.ByteOrder.tier_rationale: Tier B: exactly two legal values, and the template branches on the first character to switch the endianness of every CIFF field that follows, so both must be emitted.
APP0.ByteOrder.description: Canon CIFF byte-order word at the start of the CIFF header: 'II' for little-endian (Intel), 'MM' for big-endian (Motorola).
APP0.ByteOrder.notes: The template compares the two bytes against "II" and "MM" in the APP0 flavour lookahead at line 1148 and then calls LittleEndian() when the first byte is 'I' at line 1156, restoring BigEndian() at line 1165. This is the TIFF/EXIF byte-order convention reused by CIFF.

APP0.HeaderLength.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template uses this word as an offset -- cDirOffset = HeaderLength + cifOffset at line 1162 -- and derives the directory size from it at line 1163; a wrong value makes it parse the CIFF directory from the wrong place, so every record in it is mis-read.
APP0.HeaderLength.description: Byte length of the CIFF header, i.e. the offset from the start of the APP0 payload to the first CIFF directory block.
APP0.HeaderLength.algorithm: byte offset from the APP0 payload start (local cifOffset = FTell() at line 1153) to the directory block; cDirSize is then szSection - 2 - HeaderLength (line 1163). CIFF V1R04 fixes the header at 24 bytes: ByteOrder(2) + HeaderLength(4) + type(4) + subtype(4) + version(4) + subversion(4) + reserved(2)
APP0.HeaderLength.covers: the CIFF header, from the APP0 payload start up to the directory block
APP0.HeaderLength.notes: Byte order follows APP0.ByteOrder (LittleEndian() is set at line 1156 before this word is read), so endianness is 'n/a' here and is decided by that field.

APP0.type.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP0.type.description: First half of the CIFF header's 8-byte type signature, always the ASCII string 'HEAP'; the template's own comment states the required value.
APP0.type.notes: The lookahead at line 1149 compares eight bytes at FTell() + 6 against "HEAPJPGM", covering this field and APP0.subtype together; the value recorded here is that full eight-byte string, of which 'HEAP' is this field's four bytes. Pinned Tier A because it is a magic signature: the APP0 flavour is chosen by it, and a wrong value sends the segment to the unknown branch at line 1170.

APP0.subtype.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP0.subtype.description: Second half of the CIFF header's type signature, always the ASCII string 'JPGM'; the template's own comment states the required value.
APP0.subtype.notes: Same eight-byte lookahead as APP0.type: line 1149 compares "HEAPJPGM" at FTell() + 6, of which 'JPGM' is this field's four bytes. Together the two fields identify a Canon CIFF heap inside APP0.

APP1.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
APP1.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian APP1 marker (0xFFE1) that opens the EXIF or XMP application segment; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1596.
APP1.marker.notes: M_APP1 = 0xFFE1 is defined in enum tagID at line 144 with the comment 'Exif marker'. Exif 2.2 requires the APP1 EXIF segment to follow the APP0 JFIF segment when both are present.

APP1.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
APP1.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
APP1.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; every EXIF offset in the segment is relative to the TIFF header captured in local offset at line 1180, and the segment ends at offset + szSection - 8
APP1.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the whole APP1 payload: the identifier, and then either the TIFF/EXIF structure (6 + szSection - 8 bytes, with the template seeking to offset + szSection - 8 at line 1229 to resynchronise), or the XMP packet (szSection - 31 bytes at line 1234), or szSection - 2 unknown bytes (line 1237)
APP1.szSection.notes: Maximum 65535 because the field is a WORD, which is why long XMP packets are split across several APP1 segments in real files. The EXIF structure itself has no length field, so this word is the only bound the template has on it.

APP1.EXIF.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP1.EXIF.description: Six-byte identifier at the start of the APP1 payload: 'Exif' followed by two NUL bytes. The TIFF header begins immediately after it.
APP1.EXIF.notes: The lookahead at line 1178 compares only the first five bytes ("Exif\0") through the template's ReadStringN helper, then the field itself is read as six bytes at line 1179; Exif 2.2 requires both trailing bytes to be NUL. Pinned Tier A because it is the segment's magic identifier: without it the APP1 payload is treated as unknown (line 1237) and no EXIF structure is parsed at all.

APP1.align.tier_rationale: Tier B: exactly two legal values and the template branches on the first byte to switch the byte order of the whole EXIF block, so both must be emitted -- dropping one would delete an entire endianness path from the population.
APP1.align.description: TIFF byte-order word at the start of the EXIF structure: 'II' (0x4949) selects little-endian, 'MM' (0x4D4D) selects big-endian for every EXIF field that follows.
APP1.align.notes: The template tests align[0]=='I' at line 1182 to call LittleEndian() and restores BigEndian() at line 1230. Because the surrounding JPEG is big-endian (BigEndian() at line 1535), 'MM' is the value that keeps the EXIF block in the file's own byte order and 'II' deliberately crosses it.

APP1.tagMark.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the TIFF magic number; a TIFF/EXIF reader that does not see 42 immediately after the byte-order word rejects the structure, so the whole EXIF block is unreadable.
APP1.tagMark.description: TIFF tag mark, always 42 (0x002A) in the byte order selected by APP1.align; the template's own comment states the value.
APP1.tagMark.notes: Endianness is decided by APP1.align, not by the file's big-endian default: 'II' means this word is stored little-endian as 2A 00, 'MM' as 00 2A. TIFF 6.0 fixes the value at 42; the template comment on line 1183 records it as '// 0x002a'.

APP1.offsetFirstIFD.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template compares this word against the literal 8 at line 1185 and seeks to offset + offsetFirstIFD when it differs; a wrong value makes the first IFD be parsed from arbitrary bytes, so the whole EXIF block is mis-read.
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.description: Offset in bytes from the start of the TIFF header to the first image file directory.
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.algorithm: byte offset from the TIFF header (local offset at line 1180); the TIFF header itself is 8 bytes (align(2) + tagMark(2) + offsetFirstIFD(4)), so the canonical and by far the most common value is 8, which the template special-cases by not seeking at all (line 1185)
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.covers: position of the first IFD, not a byte count
APP1.offsetFirstIFD.notes: TIFF 6.0 requires the value to be at least 8 and to point at a valid IFD inside the same TIFF structure; values greater than 8 mean private data is wedged between the header and the first IFD. Byte order follows APP1.align.

APP1.imageData.tier_rationale: Tier C: an opaque byte run whose meaning is decided by another field. As raw bytes it is free; the one case where it must be structured is carried as a dependency, which is where a format rule belongs rather than as a cap on this field.
APP1.imageData.description: EXIF thumbnail image bytes, read at offset + thumbOffset for thumbLength bytes; the extent comes from the ThumbnailLength/StripByteCounts and ThumbnailOffset/StripOffsets tags of the thumbnail IFD.
APP1.imageData.notes: Asked the checklist question -- what must be inside this byte array? -- the answer is conditional: when the thumbnail IFD's Compression tag is 6 the template does not read imageData at all and instead parses a complete nested JPGFILE bounded by thumbLength (lines 1219-1223); for any other Compression value these raw bytes are the thumbnail (an uncompressed strip or a TIFF-encoded image), and nothing validates them. Both thumbOffset and thumbLength are locals filled from EXIF tags at lines 1206-1213 and must both be nonzero for the branch to be taken (line 1216).

APP1.XAP.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP1.XAP.description: Twenty-nine-byte XMP namespace identifier that opens an Adobe XMP packet carried in APP1; the packet's XML follows it.
APP1.XAP.notes: The lookahead at line 1231 compares all 29 bytes through the template's ReadStringN helper. Pinned Tier A because it is a magic identifier: with any other prefix the APP1 payload falls through to the unknown branch at line 1237. The XML packet that follows is free-form text (char remain[szSection - 31] at line 1234).

APP2.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
APP2.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian APP2 marker (0xFFE2) that opens the FlashPix or ICC profile application segment; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1599.
APP2.marker.notes: M_APP2 = 0xFFE2 is defined in enum tagID at line 145. ICC.1 in JPEG uses APP2 with the 'ICC_PROFILE\0' prefix; multi-block profiles emit one APP2 per block.

APP2.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
APP2.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
APP2.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; the template derives each flavour's payload extent from this field
APP2.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the whole APP2 payload: 5 + 1 + (szSection - 8) bytes for the FlashPix flavour (line 1248), 12 + 2 + (szSection - 16) bytes for the ICC flavour (line 1254), or szSection - 2 unknown bytes (line 1257)
APP2.szSection.notes: Maximum 65535 because the field is a WORD. An ICC profile larger than 65519 bytes must be split across several APP2 segments, each with its own block_num and a shared block_total.

APP2.FPXR.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP2.FPXR.description: Five-byte FlashPix identifier at the start of an APP2 payload carrying FlashPix extension data.
APP2.FPXR.notes: The lookahead at line 1245 compares the five bytes through the template's ReadStringN helper. Pinned Tier A because it is a magic identifier that selects this APP2 flavour; any other prefix routes the segment to the ICC test at line 1250 or the unknown branch at line 1257.

APP2.version.tier_rationale: Tier C: the template reads the byte and never compares it, and no JPEG decoder inspects FlashPix data at all, so pinning it would cost diversity and buy no depth. It is a version field that no decoder validates, which is exactly the case the tier test puts outside Tier A.
APP2.version.description: Version byte that follows the FPXR identifier in a FlashPix APP2 segment.
APP2.version.notes: The remaining FlashPix bytes are read as char remain[szSection - 8] at line 1248 with no further interpretation (the template's own comment on line 1249 says 'Unknown FPXR').

APP2.ICC_PROFILE.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP2.ICC_PROFILE.description: Twelve-byte identifier that marks an APP2 segment as one block of an embedded ICC colour profile; two block-numbering bytes and the profile fragment follow it.
APP2.ICC_PROFILE.notes: The lookahead at line 1250 compares all twelve bytes through the template's ReadStringN helper. Pinned Tier A because it is a magic identifier and because libjpeg-turbo's jpeg_read_icc_profile() requires exactly this prefix on every APP2 block it accepts; without it the segment is treated as unknown at line 1257 and no colour-management code runs.

APP2.block_num.tier_rationale: Tier C: a count that a size-conscious author would pin to 1, but the whole point of the field is that a profile may be split into up to 255 blocks, and each split size drives the decoder's reassembly loop differently. Only the relation to block_total is a format rule, and it is recorded as a dependency.
APP2.block_num.description: One-based sequence number of this APP2 block within a multi-block ICC profile.
APP2.block_num.notes: ICC.1 in JPEG numbers the blocks 1..block_total; libjpeg-turbo's jpeg_read_icc_profile() rejects the profile if the numbers are duplicated, missing or out of the 1..block_total span, and silently drops colour management when it does.

APP2.block_total.tier_rationale: Tier C: the repeat count for the profile's block chain. Leaving it free is what allows the population to contain single-block and many-block profiles, which exercise the reassembly loop differently; capping it at 1 would delete that path for no depth.
APP2.block_total.description: Total number of APP2 blocks that make up the embedded ICC profile.
APP2.block_total.notes: Must equal the number of APP2 ICC blocks actually present and must be identical in every one of them; that agreement is a format rule and is carried as a dependency.

APP2.data.tier_rationale: Tier A payload well-formedness: the bytes are one fragment of an ICC profile, and a reader that cannot validate the profile header discards the whole profile, so none of the colour-management code runs. The fragment's framing is pinned; the profile's contents are not.
APP2.data.description: The szSection - 16 bytes of profile data carried by this APP2 ICC block; concatenated in block_num order across all blocks they must form one complete ICC profile.
APP2.data.codec: ICC colour profile (ICC.1:2004-10 / ISO 15076-1), transported in JPEG by the 'ICC_PROFILE\0' APP2 convention
APP2.data.must_produce: The concatenation of all APP2 blocks in block_num order must be a single ICC profile: (1) a 128-byte header, big-endian throughout, with the profile size in bytes at offset 0..3 equal to the total concatenated length, preferred CMM type at 4..7, profile version at 8..11 (e.g. 02 10 00 00 for 2.1), device class at 12..15 ('mntr', 'scnr', 'prtr'), colour space at 16..19 ('RGB ', 'GRAY', 'CMYK'), profile connection space at 20..23 ('XYZ '), date and time at 24..35, the file signature 'acsp' at 36..39, platform at 40..43, flags at 44..47, device manufacturer at 48..51, device model at 52..55, device attributes at 56..63, rendering intent at 64..67, PCS illuminant (nCIEXYZ D50: 0000F6D6 00010000 0000D32D) at 68..79, profile creator at 80..83, profile MD5 at 84..99 and four reserved zero bytes at 100..127; (2) immediately after the header a uint32 tag count, then that many 12-byte tag entries (4-byte tag signature, 4-byte offset from the start of the profile, 4-byte element size), with every offset and size landing inside the concatenated profile; (3) the tag data itself. Offsets are absolute within the reassembled profile, not within one APP2 block, which is what makes the block ordering load-bearing.
APP2.data.decoder_gate: libjpeg-turbo's jpeg_read_icc_profile() walks the marker list, requires the 'ICC_PROFILE\0' prefix on every APP2 block, requires block_total to agree across blocks and block_num to cover 1..block_total exactly once, concatenates them and then validates the 128-byte header; if any step fails it returns FALSE and the caller gets no profile at all. Random bytes in this array therefore never reach the tag-table walk, the colour-transform setup or any of the ICC-aware conversion code -- the decoder skips colour management entirely and the file is decoded as plain JFIF/Adobe colour. It is not a front gate for the image itself: the scan still decodes, which is why this entry is worth having but is second in value to JPGFILE.scanData.
APP2.data.generation_strategy: Build the profile once and split it, never the other way round. (1) Choose the header fields freely (device class, colour space, PCS, dates, MD5) -- they are all content, and content_is_free below says so. (2) Emit the 128-byte header with 'acsp' at offset 36 and the D50 illuminant triple at 68..79, leaving the size field at 0..3 as a placeholder. (3) Emit a uint32 tag count and that many 12-byte tag entries; a single 'desc' tag is enough to make the structure real, and any number of further tags ('rTRC', 'gTRC', 'bTRC', 'wtpt', 'cprt') may be added freely. (4) Emit the tag data after the tag table, recording each element's absolute offset from the start of the profile as you go. (5) Patch the size field at 0..3 with the total byte count, big-endian. (6) Split the finished profile into fragments of at most 65535 - 16 = 65519 bytes each, and emit one APP2 segment per fragment with marker FFE2, szSection = 16 + fragment length, 'ICC_PROFILE\0', block_num = the fragment's 1-based index, block_total = the fragment count, then the fragment bytes. A single-fragment profile (block_num = 1, block_total = 1) is the simplest correct form and is enough to make the decoder accept the profile; varying the fragment size and count is free diversity on top of it.
APP2.data.notes: The template itself treats these bytes as opaque (char data[szSection - 16] at line 1254) and says nothing about their contents, which is exactly the case the extraction brief flags as the most often missed: an opaque array that must hold an encoded structure. derives_from lists the fields whose values this payload must agree with -- the fragment length, the block index and the block count. Those three are not to be narrowed to suit a fixed profile; the profile is split to suit them.

APP12.len.tier_rationale: Tier A: the loop bound s is decremented by sizeof(entry), which is computed from this field (line 1303); a wrong len makes the entry chain overrun or underrun the segment, so the rest of APP12 is mis-parsed and the marker that follows it is missed.
APP12.len.description: Byte count of this Ducky entry's value, i.e. the bytes that follow the len field.
APP12.len.algorithm: byte count of the entry value; excludes the 2-byte tag and the 2-byte len field, so a complete entry occupies 4 + len bytes. APP12.value.tier_rationale: Tier C: a metadata integer no JPEG decoder reads; every value parses identically, so constraining it would only make the population less varied.

APP12.count.tier_rationale: Tier C: a count whose only real relation is to len, and that relation is a dependency, not a cap. Leaving the number free keeps comment and copyright blocks of every size in the population.
APP12.count.description: Byte count that precedes a Ducky DK_Comment or DK_Copyright entry's text; the text itself occupies len - 4 bytes.
APP12.count.notes: Declared once for DK_Comment (line 1289) and again for DK_Copyright (line 1293); both branches then read char comment[len - 4].

APP12.comment.tier_rationale: Tier C: free-form text. Its extent is derived from len, so there is nothing to constrain here except the length relation, which lives in the dependency section.
APP12.comment.description: Text of a Ducky DK_Comment or DK_Copyright entry.
APP12.comment.notes: Declared once for DK_Comment (line 1290) and again for DK_Copyright (line 1294), both as char comment[len - 4].

APP13.type.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value set the template tests explicitly, each accepted value continuing the block loop, so all four are recorded.
APP13.type.description: Four-byte signature that opens each Photoshop image-resource block; '8BIM' is the normal one and the other three are the documented variants from other Adobe products.

APP13.tag.tier_rationale: Tier B: an exhaustive twelve-member enum declared in the template. Every id names a different resource, so none is dropped; the ids outside this enum are also accepted by the parser, which simply reads size bytes of uninterpreted data.
APP13.tag.description: Photoshop image-resource block id, selecting what the block's data means.
APP13.tag.notes: Declared as an anonymous enum <uint16> at lines 1328-1341. The template does not switch on this field -- it reads namelen/name/size/data identically for every id -- so the enum is a naming aid rather than a control-flow gate. Partial in effect only because Photoshop defines further ids (0x0400-0x0fff and 0x07d0-0x0bb8 ranges) that this template leaves unnamed; the set listed is exactly the set the template names.

APP13.namelen.tier_rationale: Tier C: a count. The name it sizes is free text, so the count is free too; capping it would make every IRB block carry the same shape. The only rules that apply are the parity padding and the relation to the name's extent, and both are dependencies.
APP13.namelen.description: Length in bytes of the optional Pascal-style name that follows the block id in a Photoshop image-resource block.
APP13.namelen.notes: A zero namelen means no name bytes at all (line 1343). The template then adds a padding byte when namelen is even so the block stays 2-byte aligned (lines 1345-1346) -- note that it tests namelen % 2 != 1, i.e. it pads on even lengths including zero.

APP13.name.tier_rationale: Tier C: free-form text whose extent is derived from namelen, so there is nothing here to constrain.
APP13.name.description: Optional name bytes of a Photoshop image-resource block.
APP13.name.notes: Read only when namelen is nonzero (line 1343).

APP13.padding.tier_rationale: Tier C: padding whose value is unchecked. Its presence is a parity rule, not a value rule, so the byte itself is free entropy.
APP13.padding.description: Alignment byte inserted after the block name (and, in the second declaration, after the block data) so that Photoshop image-resource blocks stay 2-byte aligned.
APP13.padding.notes: Declared twice: after the name when namelen is even (lines 1345-1346) and after the data when size is odd (lines 1350-1351). Both parities are format rules and are carried as dependencies.

APP13.size.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template reads exactly this many data bytes (line 1349) and decrements the block loop's remainsize by the resulting sizeof(block) (line 1353); a wrong size makes the block chain overrun the segment, so the rest of APP13 and the marker after it are mis-parsed.
APP13.size.description: Byte count of this image-resource block's data.
APP13.size.algorithm: byte count of char data[size]; excludes the size field itself. A zero size means no data bytes are read at all (line 1348)
APP13.size.covers: the block's data bytes that follow this field
APP13.size.notes: Photoshop IRB blocks are 2-byte aligned, so an odd size is followed by one padding byte that is not counted in size (lines 1350-1351).

APP13.data.tier_rationale: Tier C: an opaque byte run whose meaning depends on the block id. Asked the checklist question -- what must be inside? -- the answer is a per-tag sub-format that no JPEG decoder parses: libjpeg skips APP13 without looking at it, and this template reads the bytes without interpreting them. Pinning them would remove the largest free byte run in the metadata and buy no decoder depth at all.
APP13.data.description: Payload of a Photoshop image-resource block: IPTC IIM records for PS_IPTCData, an embedded thumbnail for PS_PhotoshopThumbnail, an ICC profile for PS_ICC_Profile, an XMP packet for PS_XMP, and so on.
APP13.data.notes: Read only when size is nonzero (line 1348). Where a sub-format matters to a metadata reader, the tag-to-content mapping is recorded as a dependency so the rewrite step can choose to structure it, but it is not a decoder gate and is not pinned here.

APP13.adobe_cm.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP13.adobe_cm.description: Nine-byte identifier of the Adobe colour-management APP13 flavour, an alternative to the Photoshop 3.0 identifier.

APP13.AdobeCMType.tier_rationale: Tier C: the template reads the byte and never compares it, and no JPEG decoder inspects Adobe_CM data, so pinning it would cost diversity and buy no depth. It is a type field that no decoder validates, which the tier test puts outside Tier A.
APP13.AdobeCMType.description: Type byte of the Adobe_CM APP13 flavour.

APP14.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian APP14 marker (0xFFEE) that opens the Adobe DCT-filter segment; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1608.
APP14.marker.notes: M_APP14 = 0xFFEE is defined in enum tagID at line 157. The template cites Adobe Technical Note 5116 (5116.DCT_Filter.pdf) at line 1371 for this segment.

APP14.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.

APP14.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; the template derives any trailing unknown extent from it as szSection + startof(szSection) - FTell() at line 1377
APP14.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the whole APP14 payload: 5 identifier bytes + 2 version + 2 flag0 + 2 flag1 + 1 colour-transform byte = 12 bytes, or szSection - 2 unknown bytes for a non-Adobe APP14 (line 1380)
