APP14.adobe.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the segment's identifying magic string; a decoder matches on it to decide which sub-format the segment carries, and a wrong value sends the whole segment down the unrecognised branch.
APP14.adobe.description: Five-byte identifier that marks an APP14 segment as an Adobe DCT-filter segment; the version, flag and colour-transform fields follow it.
APP14.adobe.notes: The lookahead at line 1370 compares five bytes with no trailing NUL through the template's ReadStringN helper. Pinned Tier A because it is a magic identifier and because libjpeg keys its Adobe handling on exactly these bytes: without them cinfo->saw_Adobe_marker stays FALSE and the colour-space decision that depends on color_transform_code is never taken.

APP14.version.tier_rationale: Tier B: a one-member legal set. It is recorded as an enumeration rather than pinned Tier A because libjpeg reads the word and does not validate it -- a wrong version does not make the decoder refuse the file, which is precisely the test that keeps a field out of Tier A.
APP14.version.description: Adobe APP14 format version; Adobe Technical Note 5116 defines exactly one value, 100.
APP14.version.notes: Adobe TN 5116, cited by the template at line 1371, specifies version = 100 for the APP14 DCT-filter segment. libjpeg's get_app14 stores the transform code and discards the version.

APP14.flag0.tier_rationale: Tier C: Adobe TN 5116 assigns meanings to individual bits of this word, but libjpeg's get_app14 reads it and discards it -- only the version and the colour-transform code are kept -- and this template never compares it. Nothing gates on the value, so all 65536 patterns are free and pinning any of them would only reduce diversity.
APP14.flag0.notes: This is a documented close call: a flag word normally belongs in Tier B, but the tier test is about what a decoder does with a wrong value, and here the answer is 'nothing at all'. Left free deliberately.

APP14.flag1.tier_rationale: Tier C: same reasoning as flag0 -- defined bit meanings in Adobe TN 5116, but no validation in libjpeg and none in this template, so every bit pattern parses identically and the field stays free.
APP14.flag1.notes: Left free deliberately for the same reason as flag0.

APP14.color_transform_code.tier_rationale: Tier B: a three-value code that libjpeg branches on to choose the JPEG colour space, so all three are recorded and none dropped -- each one selects a different colour-conversion routine at output time.
APP14.color_transform_code.description: Adobe colour-transform code: 0 = unknown (RGB for 3 components, CMYK for 4), 1 = YCbCr, 2 = YCCK.
APP14.color_transform_code.notes: libjpeg stores this byte as cinfo->Adobe_transform and uses it in default_jpeg_colorspace: with three components, transform 0 gives JCS_RGB and 1 gives JCS_YCbCr; with four components, 0 gives JCS_CMYK and 1 or 2 give JCS_YCCK; other values make libjpeg abort with JERR_BAD_J_COLORSPACE ('Bogus JPEG colorspace') before any pixel is produced. Values 3..255 are therefore excluded rather than enumerated. Adobe TN 5116 defines exactly 0, 1 and 2.

SOS.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
SOS.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian SOS marker (0xFFDA) that opens a scan header; the entropy-coded data begins immediately after this segment ends.

extra_evidence.snippet: M_SOS,// Start Of Scan (begins compressed data)

SOS.marker.notes: M_SOS = 0xFFDA is defined in enum tagID at line 137 with the comment 'Start Of Scan (begins compressed data)'. The template's dispatch case at line 1550 reads the header and then hunts forward for EOI with FindFirst at line 1553, treating everything in between as scan data.

SOS.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
SOS.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
SOS.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + 1 + 2*SOS.nr_comp + 3 = 6 + 2*Ns, where Ns is the number of scan components; T.81 clause B.2.3 gives Ls = 2*Ns + 6 with the same arithmetic
SOS.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the scan header: 1 byte nr_comp + 2 bytes per scan component + 4 bytes of spectral-selection and successive-approximation fields
SOS.szSection.notes: The scan header has no trailing unknown field in this template, so szSection must match the component count exactly or the template reads Ss/Se/Ah/Al from the wrong bytes. For a baseline single-scan image Ns equals SOFx.nr_comp.

SOS.nr_comp.tier_rationale: Tier B: T.81 clause B.2.3 restricts Ns to 1..4 for the DCT-based processes, and libjpeg branches on the count to pick its MCU layout, its h2v1/h2v2 upsampler and its single-component fast path. All four values are recorded so every one of those branches stays reachable.
SOS.nr_comp.description: Ns: the number of image components in this scan; it sizes the COMPSOS array that follows and decides how many blocks each MCU contains.
SOS.nr_comp.notes: Partial only because T.81 permits Ns up to 255 in principle while defining scan semantics for at most four components in the DCT processes; libjpeg's own hard cap is MAX_COMPS_IN_SCAN and its colour-space logic handles 1, 3 and 4. Values above 4 are excluded because no conforming decoder has a scan layout for them -- they abort the file rather than reach any new code. Ns must be <= SOFx.nr_comp, and for a baseline (SOF0) or extended-sequential (SOF1) image it must equal it, because those processes put every frame component in the single scan. That rule is a dependency.

COMPSOS.compId.tier_rationale: Tier A: this byte must name a component the frame header actually declared. libjpeg's get_sos searches the frame's component list for the id and aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_BAD_COMPONENT_ID) -- 'Invalid component Id' -- when it is absent, which happens before any entropy decoding, so the whole scan is lost.
COMPSOS.compId.description: Cs: identifier of this scan component, taken from the component the frame header declared.
COMPSOS.compId.algorithm: mirror of SOFx.COMPS.compId for the same component: the scan's component list is a subset (for baseline, the whole set in frame order) of the frame's component identifiers, so the generator must reuse the ids it wrote into the SOF. Never invent an id here and never narrow COMPS.compId to suit a fixed scan header
COMPSOS.compId.covers: the Cs byte of this COMPSOS entry
COMPSOS.compId.notes: Same derive-don't-shrink pattern the entropy payload uses: the free field is COMPS.compId (Tier C, any unique value) and this one is derived from it. libjpeg also requires the ids inside one scan to be distinct.

COMPSOS.AC.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value selector defined by T.81 clause B.2.3; libjpeg indexes its four AC table slots with it and aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE) -- 'No Huffman table loaded' -- when the selected slot is empty, so all four values are recorded.
COMPSOS.AC.description: Tda: AC Huffman table destination selector for this scan component -- the high nibble of the component-specification byte.
COMPSOS.AC.notes: BitfieldLeftToRight() (lines 56-57) puts this 4-bit field in the high nibble and DC in the low nibble, matching T.81's byte layout Tda<<4 | Tdc. A 4-bit field cannot hold 4..15, so the enumeration is exhaustive. For a lossless (SOF3) scan, or a progressive DC-only scan, no AC table is used and the selector is ignored.

COMPSOS.DC.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value selector defined by T.81 clause B.2.3; libjpeg indexes its four DC table slots with it and aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE) when the slot is empty, so all four are recorded.
COMPSOS.DC.description: Tdc: DC Huffman table destination selector for this scan component -- the low nibble of the component-specification byte.
COMPSOS.DC.notes: Low nibble of the same byte as COMPSOS.AC. Every scan component needs a DC table in every scan, including progressive DC-refinement scans, so the DHT that defines it must appear earlier in the file.

SOS.Ss.tier_rationale: Tier B: a bounded selector whose legal set is exactly the 64 DCT coefficient positions, each of which sends libjpeg down a different progressive-scan path. All 64 are recorded; the per-process narrowing is a dependency, not a shrink of this set.
SOS.Ss.description: Start of spectral selection: the first DCT coefficient this scan carries. For baseline and extended-sequential DCT it must be 0; for progressive DCT it selects the coefficient window; for the lossless process it carries the predictor selection 1..7 instead.
SOS.Ss.notes: libjpeg validates the whole (Ss, Se, Ah, Al) quadruple in start_pass_huff_decoder: for a non-progressive frame anything other than Ss=0, Se=63, Ah=0, Al=0 aborts with ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION) -- 'Invalid SOS parameters' -- before the entropy decoder is built. For a progressive frame Ss must be 0 for a DC scan and 1..63 for an AC scan. In a lossless (SOF3) scan the same byte is the predictor selector and its legal set is 1..7, which the dependency section records.

SOS.Se.tier_rationale: Tier B: same reasoning as Ss -- the legal set is the 64 coefficient positions and each window size gives libjpeg a different AC-first or AC-refinement decode loop, so all 64 are recorded and the per-process rule stays a dependency.
SOS.Se.description: End of spectral selection: the last DCT coefficient this scan carries. For baseline and extended-sequential DCT it must be 63; for progressive DCT it closes the window opened by Ss; for the lossless process it must be 0.
SOS.Se.notes: Se must satisfy Ss <= Se <= 63 for a progressive AC scan, and Se = 0 for a DC-only progressive scan and for a lossless scan. libjpeg's ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION) check covers this field too.

SOS.Ah.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-bit selector whose legal values are 0..13 per T.81 clause B.2.3 table B.3. Ah > 0 switches libjpeg from its first-scan decoders to its refinement decoders (decode_mcu_DC_refine / decode_mcu_AC_refine in jdphuff.c), which is a large and completely separate block of code, so the whole legal set is recorded.
SOS.Ah.description: Successive-approximation high bit position: 0 for a first scan of the selected coefficients, or the bit position one above the last one already sent, for a refinement scan.
SOS.Ah.notes: Values 14 and 15 are representable in the 4-bit field but not legal: T.81 limits the point transform to 13 bits of refinement, and libjpeg rejects them with ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION). For a baseline (SOF0/SOF1) scan Ah must be 0. Ah must be 0 whenever Ss is 0 and the scan is the first DC scan.

SOS.Al.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-bit selector with legal values 0..13 per T.81 clause B.2.3. It decides how many bits of each coefficient this scan carries, and therefore which of libjpeg's progressive coefficient-controller paths runs, so the whole legal set is recorded.
SOS.Al.description: Successive-approximation low bit position: the point-transform shift applied to every coefficient in this scan; in the lossless process this byte is the point transform Pt.
SOS.Al.notes: For a first scan Al is the number of low bits being withheld (0 means a complete coefficient); for a refinement scan Al = Ah - 1. For a baseline scan Al must be 0. Values 14 and 15 are representable but illegal and rejected with ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION).

UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.tier_rationale: Tier B: this is the template's catch-all for any marker its switch does not handle. A wrong value does not make a decoder refuse the file -- it changes which segment type the bytes are read as -- so the field is a pattern over the marker vocabulary, not a pinned constant.
UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.description: Two-byte marker of a segment this template does not model; the segment is then read as a length-prefixed run of unknown bytes.
UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.pattern: 0xFF followed by any byte that is (a) not 0x00 (a stuffed byte inside entropy data), (b) not 0xFF (a fill byte, skipped at line 1542), (c) not 0x01 or 0xD0..0xD7 (the standalone markers TEM and RST0..RST7, which carry no length field), and (d) not one of the markers the template's switch handles: 0xC0..0xC3, 0xC4, 0xDA, 0xDB, 0xDD, 0xDE, 0xE0..0xE2, 0xEC, 0xED, 0xEE, 0xFE, 0xF7
UNKNOWN.UnknownMarker.notes: The lookahead is the template's default-branch test: if the byte at the marker position is 0xFF the segment is parsed as an UNKNOWN length-prefixed segment, otherwise a single byte is consumed as garbage (lines 1618-1622). The full marker vocabulary the switch dispatches on is enum tagID at lines 115-163; markers that enum defines but the switch does not parse (M_JPG 0xFFC8, M_SOF5..M_SOF7, M_SOF9..M_SOF15, M_DAC 0xFFCC, M_DNL 0xFFDC, M_EXP 0xFFDF, M_RST0..M_RST7, M_APP3..M_APP11, M_APP15, M_JPG0..M_JPG15) all land here. libjpeg skips an unrecognised marker that carries a length field, but for the unsupported frame types it does recognise (SOF5..SOF7, SOF9..SOF11, SOF13..SOF15) it aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED) -- 'Unsupported JPEG process'.

UNKNOWN.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
UNKNOWN.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
UNKNOWN.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; the payload is skipped whole, so this field is the only thing that decides where the next marker is found
UNKNOWN.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus szSection - 2 unknown payload bytes (line 1410), truncated to the end of file when the declared length would run past it (line 1408)
UNKNOWN.szSection.notes: The template guards against an over-long segment: if FTell() + szSection - 2 >= JpegFileEnd it emits Warning('unknown section length pass the end of jpeg file') and reads only up to the file end (lines 1406-1408). libjpeg reacts to a length that runs past the end of file with 'Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment', so a generator should keep every segment length inside the file.

DHT.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
DHT.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian DHT marker (0xFFC4) that opens one or more Huffman table definitions; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1572.
DHT.marker.notes: M_DHT = 0xFFC4 is defined in enum tagID at line 121 with the comment 'Huffman Table'. Without a DHT for every table class a scan references, the scan cannot be decoded at all.

DHT.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
DHT.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
DHT.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + the sum of sizeof(huff_table) over every table in the segment; the template seeds local WORD huffsz = szSection - 2 at line 1417 and subtracts sizeof(huff_table) per iteration until huffsz <= 0 (line 1430)
DHT.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus one or more complete Huffman table definitions, each 1 + 16 + sum(L1..L16) bytes
DHT.szSection.notes: One DHT segment may carry several tables, and huffsz must come out exactly 0 for the tables to be laid out correctly; a length that is not the exact sum of the table sizes makes the loop read one table too many or too few.

Huffmann_Table.htInfo.tier_rationale: Tier B: a two-part selector byte. libjpeg's get_dht takes the low nibble as the table destination and the high nibble as the table class; a destination above 3 or a class above 1 makes it warn JWRN_HUFF_BAD_INDEX and skip the table, so a scan that later references that table aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE) -- 'No Huffman table loaded' -- before any entropy decoding happens.
Huffmann_Table.htInfo.description: Tc (table class: 0 = DC, 1 = AC) in the high nibble and Th (table destination, 0..3) in the low nibble.
Huffmann_Table.htInfo.notes: valid_bits is 0x1F: bits 0..3 are Th, bit 4 is Tc, and bits 5..7 must be zero. The eight valid_values are the cross product of Tc in {0,1} and Th in {0,1,2,3} -- four DC tables and four AC tables, matching libjpeg's four table slots per class. T.81 clause B.2.4.2 defines exactly these two classes, so the set is exhaustive. Unlike DQT's Pq/Tq (lines 1441-1442) the template does not split this byte into bitfields, so the mask is recorded explicitly.

Huffmann_Table.length.tier_rationale: Tier C: sixteen counts that shape the code tree. This is where table diversity comes from -- different count vectors give different code lengths, different bit consumption per MCU and different derived-table sizes inside the decoder. Capping them would collapse every file to one Huffman shape, which is exactly the diversity loss the brief warns about.
Huffmann_Table.length.description: L1..L16: the number of Huffman codes of each length 1..16 in this table; the sum is the number of symbol bytes that follow in HTV.
Huffmann_Table.length.notes: Two format rules apply and both are dependencies rather than caps: the sum of the 16 counts must not exceed 256 (a table has at most 256 symbols, and libjpeg rejects a longer one), and the counts must satisfy the Kraft inequality so the code is a prefix code -- sum over i of L(i) * 2^-i <= 1, with equality for a complete code. The template sums these bytes into local sumLen at lines 1423-1427 and uses it as HTV's extent. Emitting the T.81 Annex K standard tables verbatim satisfies both rules and is the simplest correct construction.

Huffmann_Table.HTV.tier_rationale: Tier B: the symbol values are a finite, class-dependent vocabulary. libjpeg builds its derived decode table from them and validates the result in jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl; a symbol outside the vocabulary for the table's class makes the table unusable, and a scan that selects it then aborts before any entropy decoding.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.description: The Huffman symbol bytes, in increasing code order: sum(L1..L16) bytes, one per code.
Huffmann_Table.HTV.pattern: For a DC table (htInfo high nibble 0): each symbol is SSSS in 0x00..0x0B, the magnitude category of a DC difference (T.81 table F.1). For an AC table (high nibble 1): each symbol is 0x00 (EOB, end of block), 0xF0 (ZRL, a run of exactly 16 zero AC coefficients), or RRRRSSSS with RRRR in 0..15 and SSSS in 1..10 -- i.e. 0x01..0x0A, 0x11..0x1A, ... 0xF1..0xFA. No other byte is a legal symbol. The number of symbols must equal sum(L1..L16) exactly, and the multiset must be arrangeable into a prefix code with the lengths given in Huffmann_Table.length
Huffmann_Table.HTV.notes: The extent comes from a local, not from a field: the template sums length[0..15] into local sumLen at lines 1423-1427 and declares ubyte HTV[sumLen]. Which symbols appear, and how many of each, is free as long as the multiset matches length[]; that freedom is what makes the entropy payload diverse. The T.81 Annex K tables (K.3 and K.4 for DC, K.5 and K.6 for AC) are the canonical choice and are what the payload's generation_strategy assumes, because in them DC symbol 0x00 has the 2-bit code 00 and AC symbol 0x00 (EOB) has the 4-bit code 1010. Confidence is medium rather than high because the vocabulary itself is unambiguous in T.81 tables F.1 and F.2, while libjpeg's enforcement of it varies: a progressive scan validates the DC and AC symbol ranges strictly, whereas a baseline scan is more permissive and only complains when an out-of-range code is actually used.

DQT.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
DQT.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian DQT marker (0xFFDB) that opens one or more quantization table definitions; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1575.
DQT.marker.notes: M_DQT = 0xFFDB is defined in enum tagID at line 138. A frame component whose Tqi names a table that was never defined makes libjpeg abort with JERR_NO_QUANT_TABLE when the IDCT initialiser looks the table up.

DQT.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
DQT.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
DQT.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + the sum of sizeof(qtable) over every table in the segment; the template seeds local WORD qtsz = szSection - 2 at line 1437 and subtracts sizeof(qtable) per iteration until qtsz <= 0 (line 1448)
DQT.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus one or more complete quantization tables, each 1 + 64 bytes for an 8-bit table (Pq = 0) or 1 + 128 bytes for a 16-bit table (Pq = 1)
DQT.szSection.notes: The per-table size depends on Pq, so szSection is a function of every table's precision: a segment holding one 8-bit table has szSection = 2 + 1 + 64 = 67, and one holding one 16-bit table has szSection = 2 + 1 + 128 = 131.

QuanTable.Pq.tier_rationale: Tier B: exactly two legal values, and the template branches on the value to choose between byte qTable[64] and uint16 qTable[64] (lines 1443-1446). Both are recorded because each gives a different table size and a different dequantization path in the decoder.
QuanTable.Pq.description: Quantization table element precision: 0 = 8-bit elements (64 bytes), 1 = 16-bit elements (128 bytes).
QuanTable.Pq.notes: T.81 clause B.2.4.1 defines Pq as 0 or 1, with 16-bit elements permitted for the 12-bit DCT processes; libjpeg reads a Pq=1 table and scales it for 8-bit output. Because the field is 4 bits wide, values 2..15 are representable but defined by nothing, so the enumeration of legal values is exhaustive at 0 and 1.

QuanTable.Tq.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value selector; libjpeg indexes its four quantization-table slots with it and aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_DQT_INDEX) -- 'Bogus table destination' -- for a value above 3, so all four are recorded.
QuanTable.Tq.description: Quantization table destination identifier: which of the four table slots this definition fills; each frame component's Tqi selects one of them.
QuanTable.Tq.notes: Low nibble of the same byte as Pq. Every component's SOFx.COMPS.compNr must name a slot that a DQT has filled; that rule is a dependency.

QuanTable.qTable.tier_rationale: Tier C: 64 free numbers, and one of the richest diversity sources in the whole format. Every distinct table changes every dequantized coefficient and therefore every output pixel, and libjpeg's islow IDCT has an explicit 'AC terms all zero' fast path that a different table can switch on or off. Capping these values would make every generated image numerically alike without removing a single decoder gate.
QuanTable.qTable.description: The 64 quantization values of this table, in the zig-zag order of T.81 annex K figure K.1; the element width is 8 or 16 bits depending on Pq.
QuanTable.qTable.notes: Declared twice: byte qTable[64] when Pq == 0 (line 1444) and uint16 qTable[64] otherwise (line 1446). T.81 does not forbid a zero element; libjpeg multiplies coefficients by the table when decoding, so a zero element forces that coefficient to zero rather than dividing by it. Values are read in the file's big-endian order.

DRI.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
DRI.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian DRI marker (0xFFDD) that opens the restart-interval definition; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1578.
DRI.marker.notes: M_DRI = 0xFFDD is defined in enum tagID at line 140.

DRI.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
DRI.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
DRI.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + 2 = 4, fixed: Ri is one WORD and there is nothing else in the segment, so this is the one segment length in the format with a single legal value
DRI.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the single WORD restart interval
DRI.szSection.notes: T.81 clause B.2.4.4 fixes Lr at 4. libjpeg's get_dri reads exactly two bytes of payload and treats any other length as a malformed marker.

DRI.Ri.tier_rationale: Tier C: a count that controls a repeat, and a major decoder-path switch. Ri = 0 keeps the entropy decoder in its plain MCU loop; any nonzero Ri makes libjpeg execute its whole restart machinery -- process_restart in jdhuff.c, the DC-predictor reset, the MCU-buffer flush in jdcoefct.c and the marker-resynchronisation checks. Capping this field to zero would delete that subsystem from coverage.
DRI.Ri.description: Restart interval: the number of MCU blocks between successive restart markers in every scan that follows; 0 means no restart markers at all.
DRI.Ri.notes: The value must agree with the entropy payload: with Ri = n the scan must carry a restart marker after every n MCUs, cycling RST0..RST7 (M_RST0 = 0xFFD0 at template line 133). That agreement is a dependency, and the payload is derived from Ri -- Ri is never narrowed to suit a fixed payload. libjpeg warns JWRN_MUST_RESYNC ('Corrupt JPEG data: found restart marker') when the interval does not match, and a missing restart marker makes the scan stop early.

DHP.marker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
DHP.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian DHP marker (0xFFDE) that opens the hierarchical-progression parent header; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1581.
DHP.marker.notes: M_DHP = 0xFFDE is defined in enum tagID at line 141. Hierarchical JPEG is T.81 annex E and is not implemented by libjpeg: it recognises the marker and refuses the file, so a DHP segment is only useful for exercising a decoder that does implement annex E. The template parses it, so its fields are recorded here.

DHP.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
DHP.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
DHP.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + 6 + 3*DHP.Nf = 8 + 3*Nf, the same arithmetic as SOFx.szSection because the parent header carries one id/sampling/Tq triple per component (lines 1465-1470)
DHP.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the parent frame header: 1 byte P + 2 Y + 2 X + 1 Nf + 3 bytes per component

DHP.P.tier_rationale: Tier B: T.81 clause B.2.6 restricts P to 2..16 for a hierarchical parent header, so all fifteen legal values are recorded. It is not Tier A because a conforming decoder that supports annex E reads the value and selects a sample width rather than refusing the file; libjpeg refuses the whole marker before it ever looks at this byte.
DHP.P.description: Sample precision of the parent image in a hierarchical progression, in bits per sample.
DHP.P.notes: The template declares the byte at line 1461 and never compares it, so the value set comes from T.81 clause B.2.6 table B.6 (DHP syntax), which restricts the parent-image sample precision P to 2..16; the field itself is grounded in the template, hence source 'both'.

DHP.Y.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead.
DHP.Y.description: Number of lines in the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.Y.notes: Parent-image geometry for a T.81 annex E hierarchical file; libjpeg refuses the marker itself, so this dimension is only meaningful to an annex E decoder. Left free for the same reason as SOFx.Y_image.

DHP.X.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead.
DHP.X.description: Number of samples per line in the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.X.notes: Counterpart of DHP.Y; see the note there.

DHP.Nf.tier_rationale: Tier B: the component count selects the decoder's colour-space and MCU layout, and the counts a decoder has any defined colour semantics for are 1, 3 and 4; all four are recorded so the two-component case stays reachable too.
DHP.Nf.description: Number of image components in the hierarchical parent image; it sizes the component_param array that follows.
DHP.Nf.notes: Partial for the same stated reason as SOFx.nr_comp: T.81 permits 1..255 components but defines colour semantics only for the layouts decoders implement, and libjpeg aborts with JERR_BAD_J_COLORSPACE for a count it cannot interpret, which buys no code at all. The template reads exactly Nf component_param triples (lines 1465-1470), so Nf also fixes DHP.szSection.

DHP.id.tier_rationale: Tier C: an identifier whose only rule is that it be distinct from every other component's id. The value itself is free, and leaving it free is what lets the population carry unusual but legal component numbering.
DHP.id.description: Component identifier of one component of the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.id.notes: Declared inside the anonymous struct that forms component_param[Nf] (lines 1465-1470), so the innermost enclosing typename is DHP. T.81 requires component identifiers to be distinct within a frame.

DHP.h_factor.tier_rationale: Tier B: T.81 restricts the sampling factors of the DCT processes to 1..4, and each factor selects a different upsampling path in the decoder, so all four are recorded and none dropped.
DHP.h_factor.description: Horizontal sampling factor of one component of the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.h_factor.notes: High nibble of the sampling byte (BitfieldLeftToRight at lines 56-57), matching T.81's Hi<<4 | Vi layout. libjpeg rejects a factor outside its supported span with JERR_BAD_SAMPLING ('Bogus sampling factors') during initial_setup, before any entropy decoding.

DHP.v_factor.tier_rationale: Tier B: the same four-value legal set and the same reasoning as h_factor -- each combination of horizontal and vertical factors selects a different upsampler.
DHP.v_factor.description: Vertical sampling factor of one component of the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.v_factor.notes: Low nibble of the sampling byte. Together with h_factor it decides the blocks per MCU for this component and the MCU grid arithmetic the entropy payload must match.

DHP.Tq.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value selector naming one of the four DQT slots; a value above 3 names no table and libjpeg aborts with JERR_DQT_INDEX, so all four legal values are recorded.
DHP.Tq.description: Quantization table destination selector for one component of the hierarchical parent image.
DHP.Tq.notes: Declared inside the component_param struct (lines 1465-1470). The table it names must have been defined by an earlier DQT; that rule is a dependency.

SOFx.marker.tier_rationale: Tier B: the marker is not pinned to one value because the four frame types are four different decoders. Baseline runs libjpeg's jdcoefct single-pass path, progressive runs the whole multi-scan coefficient buffer and the jdphuff entropy decoder, extended sequential allows 12-bit samples, and lossless replaces the DCT with a predictor. Narrowing this field to SOF0 would delete all of that; it is Tier B with a preferred subset, not Tier A.
SOFx.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian frame-header marker. This one struct is instantiated for four different markers, and the marker selects the compression process: SOF0 baseline DCT, SOF1 extended sequential DCT, SOF2 progressive DCT, SOF3 lossless sequential.
SOFx.marker.notes: Partial because the template's switch instantiates SOFx only for SOF0..SOF3 (lines 1584-1594); M_SOF5..M_SOF15 are defined in enum tagID at lines 122-132 but fall through to the UNKNOWN default branch, and libjpeg refuses them outright with ERREXIT1(JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED) -- 'Unsupported JPEG process'. The four values listed are therefore the complete set this struct can carry. A file must contain exactly one frame header: libjpeg aborts with JERR_SOF_DUPLICATE ('Invalid JPEG file structure: two SOF markers') on a second one.

SOFx.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
SOFx.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
SOFx.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + 6 + 3*SOFx.nr_comp = 8 + 3*Nf; T.81 clause B.2.2 gives Lf = 8 + 3*Nf with the same arithmetic. The template reads exactly that shape: precision, Y_image, X_image, nr_comp and then comp[nr_comp] (lines 1476-1486)
SOFx.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the frame header: 1 byte precision + 2 Y + 2 X + 1 nr_comp + 3 bytes per component
SOFx.szSection.notes: There is no trailing unknown field in this segment, so szSection must equal 8 + 3*Nf exactly or the component array is read from the wrong offset.

SOFx.precision.tier_rationale: Tier B: a two-value legal set for the processes this template models, and the two values select genuinely different decoders -- libjpeg's 8-bit and 12-bit sample paths use different JSAMPLE widths, different IDCT scaling and different colour-conversion routines. Both are recorded so neither path is deleted.
SOFx.precision.description: P: sample precision in bits per sample for the DCT-based processes; 8 for baseline, 8 or 12 for extended sequential and progressive.
SOFx.precision.notes: libjpeg aborts with ERREXIT1(JERR_BAD_PRECISION) -- 'Unsupported JPEG process' -- when the precision does not match the sample width it was compiled for, so this field is close to Tier A; it stays Tier B because 12 is a legal value that a 12-bit build decodes fully, and dropping it would delete that build's entire code path. For a lossless frame (SOF3) T.81 clause B.2.2 allows 2..16 instead, which the dependency section records. For SOF0 the only legal value is 8.

SOFx.Y_image.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead. This is the field the brief's GIF example was about: a decoder allocates and loops over Y * X samples, so Y drives the number of MCU rows, the number of output scanlines and every row-buffer path in between.
SOFx.Y_image.description: Y: number of lines in the frame -- the image height in pixels, before any subsampling.
SOFx.Y_image.notes: excluded_values carries the single value that is not a height: T.81 clause B.2.2 allows Y = 0 only to mean 'the number of lines is not specified', which requires a DNL segment (M_DNL = 0xFFDC, defined in enum tagID at line 139) to supply the real count later. This template does not parse DNL at all, and libjpeg aborts a zero-height image with 'Empty JPEG image (DNL not supported)', so a generator must never emit 0 here. That is a format rule about one value, not a narrowing of the remaining span: heights from 1 to 65535 all stay reachable, including heights that are not a multiple of the MCU height, which is what exercises the decoder's partial-MCU padding logic. The entropy payload is derived from this field (McuY = ceil(Y / (8*Vmax))), never the other way round.

SOFx.X_image.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead. X sets the MCU column count, the row stride of every component buffer and the number of pixels the colour converter and upsampler walk per row.
SOFx.X_image.description: X: number of samples per line in the frame -- the image width in pixels, before any subsampling.
SOFx.X_image.notes: excluded_values carries the single illegal value: T.81 clause B.2.2 requires X >= 1 (unlike Y there is no 'unspecified' encoding for the width), and libjpeg refuses a zero-width image. Every width from 1 to 65535 stays reachable, including widths that are not a multiple of the MCU width, which is what exercises the decoder's partial-MCU edge handling. The entropy payload is derived from this field (McuX = ceil(X / (8*Hmax))), never the other way round.

SOFx.nr_comp.tier_rationale: Tier B: the component count is the single biggest selector of decoder code paths after the frame type. 1 gives libjpeg the grayscale path (no colour conversion at all), 3 gives YCbCr with chroma upsampling and ycc_rgb_convert, 4 gives CMYK or YCCK with the four-plane MCU layout and ycck_cmyk_convert. All four are recorded; none is dropped.
SOFx.nr_comp.description: Nf: number of image components in the frame; it sizes the comp[] array and tells the decoder how many planes it is reconstructing.
SOFx.nr_comp.notes: Partial, with the reason stated as the schema requires: T.81 clause B.2.2 permits Nf from 1 to 255, but defines no colour semantics beyond the layouts decoders actually implement, and libjpeg's default_jpeg_colorspace aborts with JERR_BAD_J_COLORSPACE ('Bogus JPEG colorspace') for any count other than 1, 3 or 4 -- before any pixel is produced, so counts of 5 and above buy no code at all. 2 is kept because T.81 allows it and it reaches the two-component setup path before that abort. Nf fixes SOFx.szSection (8 + 3*Nf), the number of COMPS entries, the MCU layout through the sampling factors, and the number of components a baseline scan must carry.

COMPS.compId.tier_rationale: Tier C: an identifier whose only format rule is that it be distinct from every other component's id in the frame. The value is free, and the scan header derives its own ids from it -- the pairing is recorded so the rewrite step mirrors this field instead of narrowing it.
COMPS.compId.description: Ci: identifier of this frame component, referenced later by every scan header that carries the component.
COMPS.compId.notes: Declared inside struct COMPS (lines 1481-1486), so the innermost enclosing typename is COMPS. T.81 clause B.2.2 requires the identifiers to be distinct; libjpeg matches them by value when it reads a scan header and aborts with JERR_BAD_COMPONENT_ID when a scan names an id the frame never declared. Because COMPSOS.compId is derived from this field, any value works as long as the two agree -- which is exactly why this one stays free. libjpeg's colour-space guess does look at the ids (1,2,3 in order suggests YCbCr), so unusual but legal ids are a genuine diversity source rather than noise.

COMPS.Horz.tier_rationale: Tier B: T.81 clause B.2.2 restricts the DCT processes to 1..4, and libjpeg picks a different upsampler for each ratio: all-ones means no upsampling at all, 2:1 horizontal means h2v1, 2:2 means h2v2, and any other ratio falls back to the generic int_upsample path. Each of those is a separate block of code, so all four values are recorded.
COMPS.Horz.description: Hi: horizontal sampling factor of this component -- how many 8x8 blocks it contributes horizontally to one MCU.
COMPS.Horz.notes: High nibble of the sampling byte (BitfieldLeftToRight at lines 56-57), matching T.81's Hi<<4 | Vi layout. libjpeg rejects a factor outside its supported span with JERR_BAD_SAMPLING ('Bogus sampling factors') in initial_setup, before any entropy decoding, so 0 and 5..15 are outside the legal set rather than merely unenumerated. Hmax = max over components of Hi is what the MCU grid and the entropy payload are computed from: the payload derives from this field, and this field is never narrowed to suit a payload.

COMPS.Vert.tier_rationale: Tier B: the same four-value legal set as Horz, and the vertical ratio is what selects libjpeg's h2v1 versus h2v2 upsampler and its merged-upsample optimisation, so all four values are recorded.
COMPS.Vert.description: Vi: vertical sampling factor of this component -- how many 8x8 blocks it contributes vertically to one MCU.
COMPS.Vert.notes: Low nibble of the sampling byte. Vmax = max over components of Vi; together with Hmax it gives the MCU dimensions (8*Hmax by 8*Vmax) and the blocks-per-MCU count sum(Hi*Vi) that the entropy payload must match exactly. For a progressive frame (SOF2) T.81 requires every Hi and Vi to be 1, and for a lossless frame (SOF3) the same; both rules are dependencies.

COMPS.compNr.tier_rationale: Tier B: a four-value selector; libjpeg indexes its four quantization-table slots with it and aborts with JERR_NO_QUANT_TABLE when the selected slot was never filled by a DQT, so all four legal values are recorded and each must be backed by a table.
COMPS.compNr.description: Tqi: quantization table destination selector for this component -- which of the four DQT slots its 64 dequantization divisors come from.
COMPS.compNr.notes: The template names this field compNr, but positionally it is T.81's Tqi: it follows the sampling byte in the component specification and selects a quantization table, not a component number. Sharing one table between luma and chroma versus giving each its own is a real diversity axis, because the dequantized coefficients -- and therefore whether libjpeg's islow IDCT takes its 'AC terms all zero' fast path -- depend on which table a component lands on.

COMMENT.CommentMarker.tier_rationale: Tier A: the marker is the segment's identity; a decoder that does not see the expected 0xFF-prefixed marker code either refuses the file or stops parsing there, so this field can never carry a mutated value.
COMMENT.CommentMarker.description: Two-byte big-endian COM marker (0xFFFE) that opens a comment segment; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1611.
COMMENT.CommentMarker.notes: M_COMM = 0xFFFE is defined in enum tagID at line 162 with the comment 'Comment'. COM segments may appear anywhere a marker may, any number of times, and libjpeg simply skips them.

COMMENT.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
COMMENT.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
COMMENT.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + the number of comment bytes; the template reads char comment[szSection-2] at line 1492 and copies szSection-2 bytes into a NUL-terminated local buffer for printing (lines 1495-1502)
COMMENT.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the comment text
COMMENT.szSection.notes: szSection = 2 is legal and means an empty comment. The direction of derivation matters: the text is free and the length is computed from it, not the other way round.

COMMENT.comment.tier_rationale: Tier C: free-form content. It is the cheapest way to make two generated files differ, and nothing in a JPEG decoder branches on it -- libjpeg skips the segment by length. Constraining it (to printable ASCII, to a fixed length, to a set of strings) would cost diversity for exactly zero depth.
COMMENT.comment.description: The comment text itself: arbitrary bytes, not required to be text or NUL-terminated.
COMMENT.comment.notes: The template's read function copies the bytes and replaces embedded NULs with 'x' purely so it can Printf them (lines 1495-1502); that is a display convenience, not a format rule. Bytes 0x00 and 0xFF are both legal here -- a COM segment is not entropy-coded data, so no byte stuffing applies.

JPGLS.marker.description: Two-byte big-endian SOF55 marker (0xFFF7) that opens a JPEG-LS frame header; the top-level switch dispatches on it at line 1614.

JPGLS.szSection.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the marker segment's length field (T.81 clause B.1.1.4 calls it Lx); a decoder reads exactly that many bytes and then resynchronises on the next marker, so a wrong length makes it parse the following bytes as the wrong segment and the file is refused or the decode stops.
JPGLS.szSection.description: Big-endian byte count of this marker segment: the two length bytes plus the segment payload, excluding the two-byte marker itself.
JPGLS.szSection.algorithm: byte count = 2 + payload length; the template models one component slot only (C_compID, sub_sampling, Tq at lines 1514-1516) and treats everything past the first 11 bytes as unknown
JPGLS.szSection.covers: the two length bytes plus the JPEG-LS frame header: 1 precision + 2 Y + 2 X + 1 Nf + 2 bytes for the single component the template models, plus szSection - 11 further bytes when the segment is longer (line 1519)
JPGLS.szSection.notes: T.87 clause A.1 gives Lf = 8 + 2*Nf for SOF-55, i.e. 2 bytes per component (Ci and Tqi). This template reads a fixed three-byte component slot instead of looping over Nf, so for Nf > 1 the remaining components land in the uknown[szSection - 11] tail (line 1519). A generator that wants a well-formed multi-component JPEG-LS frame should follow T.87's 8 + 2*Nf arithmetic and accept that this template will show the extra components as unknown bytes.

JPGLS.precision.tier_rationale: Tier B: T.87 clause A.1 allows 2..16 bits per sample, and a T.87 decoder branches on the value to choose its sample width, its bias and threshold computation and its near-lossless scaling. All fifteen legal values are recorded so none of those branches is deleted.
JPGLS.precision.description: Bits per sample of a JPEG-LS frame; the template's own field comment names it 'bits per sample'.
JPGLS.precision.notes: Values 0, 1 and 17..255 are outside the legal set: T.87 requires PRECISION in 2..16 and CharLS rejects anything else while reading the start-of-frame marker. The template declares the byte with <comment="bits per sample"> and makes no comparison, so the value set comes from T.87 while the field itself is grounded in the template.

JPGLS.Y_numlines.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead. Note that 0 is legal here, unlike SOFx.Y_image: T.87 clause A.1 permits Y = 0 to mean 'the number of lines is not defined', so this field carries no excluded value at all.
JPGLS.Y_numlines.description: Number of lines in a JPEG-LS frame -- the image height.
JPGLS.Y_numlines.notes: Because 0 is legal there is nothing to exclude and nothing to cap: the whole WORD span is available. A T.87 decoder with Y = 0 keeps decoding scanlines until it runs out of data, which is a distinct code path from the sized case.

JPGLS.X_numcols.tier_rationale: Tier C: a dimension. It sizes the decoder's buffers and its row loops, and every distinct value is a different amount of work through the same code; pinning it to a handful of values is the documented failure mode of this task, so it is left completely free and any payload that has to agree with it is derived from it instead.
JPGLS.X_numcols.description: Number of columns in a JPEG-LS frame -- the image width.
JPGLS.X_numcols.notes: T.87 requires at least one column, but the value is otherwise free across the WORD span; the line width drives the context-modelling loop of a LOCO-I decoder.

JPGLS.Nf.tier_rationale: Tier B: the component count decides whether a T.87 decoder runs its single-component (non-interleaved) or multi-component (interleaved) code path, and how many component specifications follow, so the small legal set is recorded rather than pinned.
JPGLS.Nf.description: Number of components in a JPEG-LS frame; the template's own field comment names it 'number of components in frame'.

JPGLS.Nf.notes: Partial for the same stated reason as SOFx.nr_comp: T.87 permits more components in principle, but CharLS implements 1-, 3- and 4-component images and rejects the rest while reading the frame header, so larger counts buy no decoder path. This template reads exactly one component slot regardless of Nf (lines 1514-1516), so for Nf > 1 the remaining component specifications fall into the unknown tail at line 1519.

JPGLS.C_compID.tier_rationale: Tier C: an identifier whose only rule is distinctness from the other components' ids. Leaving it free costs nothing and keeps unusual-but-legal component numbering in the population.
JPGLS.C_compID.description: Component identifier of the (single) component slot this template models in a JPEG-LS frame.
JPGLS.C_compID.notes: T.87 clause A.1 requires component identifiers to be distinct within a frame; nothing validates the specific values.

JPGLS.sub_sampling.tier_rationale: Tier B: a small selector whose values choose between a T.87 decoder's interleaved and non-interleaved line loops, so the four values are recorded; it is not Tier A because the template makes no comparison against it.
JPGLS.sub_sampling.description: Second byte of the component slot in this template's JPEG-LS frame header. Read as the interleave mode ILV it selects how a multi-component JPEG-LS scan is laid out: 0 = line interleaved, 1..3 = sample interleaved with 2, 3 or 4 components.
JPGLS.sub_sampling.notes: Recorded with low confidence and an explicit ambiguity, because the template's field name does not match T.87's layout. T.87 clause A.1 gives each SOF-55 component specification as Ci followed by Tqi (two bytes) and puts the interleave mode ILV in the JPEG-LS preset parameters (LSE) segment, not in the frame header. This template reads three bytes for one component (C_compID, sub_sampling, Tq at lines 1514-1516), so the byte named sub_sampling is either the author's reading of ILV or the component's Tqi. Both readings agree that 0 is the ordinary value, and the four values listed are the legal ILV codings of T.87 table A.1; if the byte is in fact Tqi then T.87 requires it to be 0 for the lossless process, which the dependency section records.

JPGLS.Tq.tier_rationale: Tier A: the template's own field comment states the required value -- 'always 0'. JPEG-LS has no quantization tables, so a T.87 decoder that finds a nonzero table destination in a SOF-55 frame header has nothing to apply and refuses the frame.
JPGLS.Tq.description: Quantization table destination in a JPEG-LS frame header; JPEG-LS is not quantized, so this byte is always zero.

JPGLS.Tq.notes: The evidence is the template's own inline attribute: uchar Tq <comment="always 0">. T.87 clause A.1 includes Tqi in the component specification and requires it to be 0 for the lossless process, which is the only process a SOF-55 header describes. This is the one field in the JPEG-LS structure whose value the template states explicitly.

JPGFILE.SOIMarker.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the file's opening magic number. libjpeg reads the first two bytes and aborts with JERR_NO_SOI -- 'Not a JPEG file: starts with 0x%02x 0x%02x' -- if they are not FFD8, having executed nothing but the read. This template's loop starts at the same position and dispatches on the same word (lines 1544-1549).
JPGFILE.SOIMarker.description: Start Of Image: the two-byte big-endian marker that must be the very first thing in the file.
JPGFILE.SOIMarker.notes: M_SOI = 0xFFD8 is defined in enum tagID at line 135 with the comment 'Start Of Image'. The dispatch case is at line 1546 and the file must contain exactly one SOI: libjpeg aborts with JERR_SOF_DUPLICATE-style structure errors on a second frame-level marker and treats a second SOI as invalid structure. The 0xFF fill-byte skip at line 1542 runs before every marker including this one, so a file may in principle be preceded by 0xFF fill bytes and still be parsed by this template -- libjpeg, however, requires FFD8 at offset 0.

JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.tier_rationale: Tier C: this branch exists only to describe a broken file. A generator should never take it -- the structure section requires EOI -- so there is nothing here to constrain and nothing to gain by constraining it.
JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.description: Fallback field the template uses when FindFirst cannot locate an EOI marker after a scan header: everything from the end of the SOS header to the end of file is taken as truncated scan data.

JPGFILE.unterminatedScanData.notes: Asked the checklist question -- what must be inside this byte array? -- the answer is 'the same entropy-coded data as scanData, but cut short before any EOI'. libjpeg handles a missing EOI by decoding what it has and then warning JWRN_HIT_MARKER ('Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment'), filling the remaining MCUs with mid-grey. That is a shallower parse than a complete file, not a deeper one, so the generator must always emit JPGFILE.EOIMarker instead of relying on this field. The template prints 'Missing End of File marker' at line 1557 when it takes this branch.

JPGFILE.scanData.tier_rationale: Tier A payload well-formedness: this is the compressed image data itself. The template declares it as an opaque byte run whose extent is 'up to the next EOI', and says nothing about its contents -- but if the bytes are not a valid Huffman-coded scan, libjpeg stops inside the first MCU row and none of the decode pipeline runs. This is the single most valuable entry in the file.
JPGFILE.scanData.description: The entropy-coded segment: every byte between the end of the SOS header and the EOI marker, found by the template with FindFirst(M_EOI, ...) at line 1553 and read as char scanData[fpos2 - FTell()] at line 1561.

JPGFILE.scanData.codec: JPEG Huffman-coded entropy data -- ITU-T T.81 annex F for baseline and extended sequential DCT, annex G for progressive DCT, annex H for the lossless process -- with 0xFF byte stuffing per clause F.1.2.3 and optional RSTn restart markers per clause F.2.1.3
JPGFILE.scanData.must_produce: A contiguous bit stream, running from the end of the SOS header to the EOI marker, that decodes under the Huffman tables named in that SOS header into exactly the number of MCUs the frame geometry implies. Concretely, in order: (1) for each MCU in raster order and for each component of the scan, that component's Hi*Vi blocks, MSB-first and bit-packed across byte boundaries; (2) for each block, a DC code taken from the DC table selected by COMPSOS.DC -- the symbol is SSSS, the magnitude category of the DC *difference* from that component's previous DC value, followed by SSSS magnitude bits, with a negative difference V of category S written as V + (2^S - 1); (3) for a baseline or extended-sequential scan, the AC codes from the table selected by COMPSOS.AC -- each nonzero coefficient as RRRRSSSS (RRRR preceding zeros, SSSS magnitude bits), a run of exactly 16 zeros as ZRL 0xF0, and the end of the block as EOB 0x00; (4) for a progressive scan, only the coefficients in the Ss..Se window, with the successive-approximation rules for Ah/Al: a first scan (Ah=0) sends SSSS magnitudes with the Al low bits withheld, a refinement scan (Ah>0) sends one correction bit per already-sent coefficient plus the EOB run codes, whose low nibble carries the zero-run length; (5) byte stuffing per T.81 clause F.1.2.3: every 0xFF data byte must be followed by an inserted 0x00, so that no 0xFF appears in the scan data unless it is a stuffing byte or a real marker; (6) the final partial byte filled with 1 bits, and stuffed with 0x00 if that makes it 0xFF; (7) when DRI.Ri is nonzero, a restart marker 0xFFD0+n after every Ri MCUs with n cycling 0..7, the DC predictors reset to zero and the bit position realigned to a byte boundary before the marker.
JPGFILE.scanData.decoder_gate: This is the highest-value gate in the format. Random bytes here fail in three separate ways, and all three are shallow. (a) A bit sequence that is not a code in the selected table makes libjpeg's jpeg_huff_decode warn JWRN_HUFF_BAD_CODE ('Corrupt JPEG data: bad Huffman code') and substitute a zero symbol, so every coefficient decodes as 0 and the image comes out flat. (b) The first 0xFF byte that is not followed by 0x00 is read as a marker, which ends the entropy-coded segment: libjpeg's jpeg_consume_input stops there, reports a restart-marker mismatch through JWRN_MUST_RESYNC or, when the MCU count comes up short, JWRN_HIT_MARKER ('Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment'), and fills the remaining blocks with mid-grey. Because a random byte is 0xFF with probability 1/255, this happens on average within the first few hundred bytes -- so in effect nothing below the first MCU row is ever decoded, and the whole back half of the pipeline (jpeg_idct_islow, the h2v1/h2v2 upsamplers, ycc_rgb_convert, the output row loop) never executes. (c) If the restart interval disagrees with DRI.Ri, process_restart aborts the scan. Byte stuffing is therefore not a nicety: it is what keeps the decoder inside the scan for the whole image.
JPGFILE.scanData.generation_strategy: Emit the all-zero-coefficient image with the T.81 Annex K standard tables -- the JPEG equivalent of a deflate stored block. It is trivial to generate, always valid, and gets the decoder all the way through the pixel pipeline. Step by step: (1) Emit the Annex K tables verbatim in DHT segments: K.3 DC luminance, K.4 DC chrominance, K.5 AC luminance, K.6 AC chrominance, as htInfo 0x00, 0x01, 0x10 and 0x11. In those tables DC symbol 0x00 has the 2-bit code 00 in both DC tables, and AC EOB 0x00 has the 4-bit code 1010 in K.5 and the 2-bit code 00 in K.6. (2) Compute the MCU grid from the frame, never the other way round: Hmax = max(COMPS.Horz), Vmax = max(COMPS.Vert), McuX = ceil(SOFx.X_image / (8*Hmax)), McuY = ceil(SOFx.Y_image / (8*Vmax)), MCUs = McuX * McuY, and blocks per MCU = sum over scan components of Hi*Vi. The ceil() is the format's own padding rule and libjpeg performs the identical arithmetic, so a width or height that is not a multiple of the MCU size is fine and must not be avoided. (3) For every block append the DC code for category 0 -- the two bits 00, with no magnitude bits, because the DC difference is zero (the predictor starts at 0 and stays there) -- then the AC EOB code, which covers all 63 AC coefficients at once. That is 6 bits per luma block and 4 bits per chroma block under the Annex K tables. For the common 4:2:0 three-component frame (Y at 2x2, Cb and Cr at 1x1) one MCU is 4*6 + 2*4 = 32 bits, i.e. exactly the four bytes 0x28 0xA2 0x8A 0x00 repeated McuX*McuY times; note that 0xFF never occurs, so this construction needs no stuffing byte at all. For a one-component frame at 1x1 the same 6-bit block pattern repeats every four MCUs, giving the three bytes 0x28 0xA2 0x8A. (4) Accumulate the bits MSB-first into bytes; pad the final partial byte with 1 bits and append 0x00 if the padding makes it 0xFF. (5) If DRI.Ri = n is nonzero, emit 0xFFD0+k after every n MCUs, byte-aligned, with k cycling 0..7 and the DC predictors reset to zero at each restart. (6) Append 0xFFD9 (JPGFILE.EOIMarker). For a progressive frame the same all-zero idea applies per scan: a DC-first scan (Ss=Se=0) sends category 0 for each block, an AC-first scan sends EOB immediately for each block, and a refinement scan (Ah>0) sends a single 0 correction bit per coefficient. Diversity on top of this floor comes from the coefficients, not the geometry: give some blocks a nonzero DC category (longer codes, real magnitude bits, nonzero reconstructed pixels) or a single nonzero AC coefficient (which forces libjpeg's islow IDCT down its full 8x8 path instead of its 'AC terms all zero' fast path), and vary Ri, the sampling factors, the component count, the quantization tables, the Huffman table shapes, the spectral windows and the number of scans. X_image and Y_image are inputs to step 2 and must never be shrunk to make a precomputed payload fit.
JPGFILE.scanData.notes: content_is_free is true and that is the whole point of the entry: the *framing* is Tier A (valid Huffman codes, correct MCU count, byte stuffing, correct restart placement) while the *coefficients inside* are unconstrained, so the file gets full depth and full diversity at once. Every field listed in derives_from is an input to the payload's shape and must stay free -- the payload is computed from the geometry, the tables and the scan header, and none of them is narrowed to suit a fixed payload. The template's own handling confirms the extent rule: it searches forward for the first EOI rather than backward (version 1.6.2 history, lines 15-17) precisely because scan data may contain bytes that look like a marker -- which is what byte stuffing prevents inside a well-formed file, and what makes the search necessary in a corrupt one.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.tier_rationale: Tier A: this is the file's closing terminator. libjpeg looks for it to finish the decode cleanly; without it the scan is treated as truncated and the decoder warns JWRN_HIT_MARKER ('Corrupt JPEG data: premature end of data segment') after filling the remaining MCUs with grey, which is a shallower parse. This template searches forward for it at line 1553 and sets bEOI at line 1567 to leave the top-level loop.
JPGFILE.EOIMarker.description: End Of Image: the two-byte big-endian marker that terminates the file.

JPGFILE.EOIMarker.notes: M_EOI = 0xFFD9 is defined in enum tagID at line 136 with the comment 'End Of Image'. It must follow the last scan's entropy data; the template's FindFirst(M_EOI, ...) at line 1553 is what fixes the extent of JPGFILE.scanData, so a missing or misplaced EOI also changes how much data the template attributes to the scan. JPGFILE.unknownPadding.tier_rationale: Tier C: trailing bytes whose value is unchecked. A JPEG decoder stops at EOI and ignores everything after it, so these bytes are free entropy -- and free file-to-file variation that costs nothing.
JPGFILE.unknownPadding.description: Bytes after the EOI marker up to the end of file; the template colours them silver to mark them as trailing padding.
JPGFILE.unknownPadding.notes: Read only when something is left after EOI (line 1565 tests JpegFileEnd - FTell()). A generator may omit them entirely; emitting them exercises nothing in libjpeg, which returns from jpeg_finish_decompress at EOI. Useful only as a cheap size/shape differentiator between generated files.

JPGFILE.garbage.tier_rationale: Tier C: the template tolerates these bytes one at a time and keeps scanning (the version 1.6.1 history entry at lines 18-19 records exactly that fix: 'Don't fail when garbage bytes are present between JPEG sections'), and libjpeg warns JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA ('Corrupt JPEG data: %ld extraneous bytes before marker') and continues. So a wrong value here does not stop anything -- it is free.

JPGFILE.garbage.notes: They must never appear inside entropy-coded data, where any 0xFF that is not followed by 0x00 ends the scan; between segments they are harmless. A generator should emit few or none, since the warning path is short, but the field is recorded because the template's default branch reads it and a rewrite step must know it exists.

dependencies.description: In a baseline (SOF0) or extended-sequential (SOF1) image the scan carries every coefficient of every block in one pass, so the spectral selection must span the whole block and there is no successive approximation.
dependencies.notes: T.81 clause B.2.3 table B.3: for the sequential DCT processes Ss and Ah shall be 0, Se shall be 63 and Al shall be 0. libjpeg enforces this in start_pass_huff_decoder and aborts with ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION) -- 'Invalid SOS parameters' -- before the entropy decoder is built, so this dependency is a hard gate for the commonest file shape in the format.

then.rule: 0 <= Ss <= Se <= 63; Ss = Se = 0 for a DC-only scan, Ss >= 1 for an AC scan

dependencies.description: A progressive (SOF2) image splits the 64 coefficients into spectral-selection windows, and each window must be a non-empty, non-overlapping, increasing range that between them covers 0..63 for every component.
dependencies.notes: T.81 annex G.2: the first scan of a component must start at Ss = 0 for the DC coefficient, and every coefficient 0..63 must be sent by exactly one first scan of that component. libjpeg checks the whole quadruple with ERREXIT4(JERR_BAD_PROGRESSION) and validates the scan order again in jdinput.c's per-pass setup.

then.rule: Ah = 0 for a first scan of the selected coefficients and Al = the number of low bits withheld; for a refinement scan Ah > 0 and Al = Ah - 1; both within 0..13

dependencies.description: Successive approximation in a progressive image: a coefficient's bits are sent in at most two passes, and the second pass must name the bit position the first one stopped at.
dependencies.notes: T.81 annex G.2. Ah > 0 switches libjpeg to its refinement decoders (decode_mcu_DC_refine and decode_mcu_AC_refine in jdphuff.c), which is a large separate block of code from the first-scan decoders.

dependencies.description: In a lossless (SOF3) image the same four bytes mean something completely different: Ss carries the predictor selection 1..7, Se must be 0, Ah must be 0, and Al carries the point transform.
dependencies.notes: T.81 clause B.2.3 and annex H.1. There are no AC coefficients at all, so the entropy payload is a run of prediction errors coded with the DC table only. libjpeg refuses lossless JPEG unless it was built with C_LOSSLESS_SUPPORTED, in which case it uses jdlhuff.c instead of jdhuff.c -- a completely separate entropy decoder.

dependencies.description: Baseline DCT is defined only for 8-bit sample precision.
dependencies.notes: T.81 clause B.2.2 table B.1: for SOF0, P shall be 8. libjpeg's get_sof records the precision and initial_setup compares it with the sample width it was compiled for, aborting with ERREXIT1(JERR_BAD_PRECISION) -- 'Unsupported JPEG process' -- on a mismatch.

dependencies.description: Extended-sequential and progressive DCT are defined for 8- or 12-bit sample precision.
dependencies.notes: T.81 clause B.2.2 table B.1: for SOF1 and SOF2, P shall be 8 or 12. A 12-bit file needs a libjpeg built for 12-bit samples and exercises a different IDCT scaling path.

dependencies.description: The lossless process is defined for 2 to 16 bits of sample precision.
dependencies.notes: T.81 clause B.2.2 table B.1: for SOF3, P shall be in 2..16.

dependencies.description: Progressive and lossless frames do not subsample: every component's horizontal and vertical sampling factors must be 1.

structure.description: The scan count is the second repeating structure and the one that decides whether libjpeg runs its single-pass or its multi-pass coefficient controller.
