Rationale: with the all-zero construction a 4:2:0 baseline scan costs 4 bytes per MCU, so 64 KiB of scan data covers images up to about 128x128 MCUs -- far more geometry than the metadata budget needs, and small enough that a fuzzer can produce many thousands of files. Progressive files split the same total across more scans. The budget bounds the total scan bytes only; it never caps X_image, Y_image or the sampling factors, which is what would have happened if the dimensions had been narrowed instead.
structure.generation_note: Emit a repeated array of (SOS header + entropy data) pairs, each pair's byte count added to a running total that is checked against the budget before the next pair is started; stop the array when the budget is reached or when every coefficient has been sent.

structure.subject: JPGFILE.scanData
structure.detail: The entropy-coded segment is contiguous and has no length prefix: it runs from the byte after the SOS header to the byte before the next marker, which the template finds by searching forward for EOI (line 1553) and reads as char scanData[fpos2 - FTell()] (line 1561). No other segment may be interleaved with it, except the restart markers RST0..RST7 that belong to it.
structure.description: This is the one part of a JPEG file that is not length-prefixed, which is why its internal framing -- byte stuffing and restart markers -- is a Tier A payload rule.
structure.output_budget: Counted against the SOS/scan budget above; the segment itself has no per-segment cap because it has no length field.
structure.generation_note: Emit the SOS header, then the bit-packed Huffman stream, then EOI. Insert RSTn markers inside the stream when DRI.Ri is nonzero. Never insert an APP or COM segment between SOS and EOI.

extra_evidence.snippet: fpos2 = FindFirst(M_EOI, true, false, FINDMETHOD_NORMAL, 0.0, 1, FTell());

structure.subject: an 0xFF byte inside JPGFILE.scanData that is not followed by 0x00
structure.detail: Inside entropy-coded data every 0xFF byte must be followed by an inserted 0x00 (T.81 clause F.1.2.3 byte stuffing). An 0xFF followed by anything else is read as a marker and ends the scan; an 0xFF followed by 0x00 is read as the data byte 0xFF.
structure.description: Without stuffing, a payload that happens to contain 0xFF loses the rest of the image, which is the most common reason a JPEG fuzzer's files decode to almost nothing.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a framing rule, not a repeating structure)
structure.generation_note: After building the bit stream, walk it and insert 0x00 after every 0xFF byte produced. The all-zero construction in JPGFILE.scanData's generation_strategy produces no 0xFF at all, which is why it is the recommended floor.

structure.subject: 0xFF fill bytes before any marker
structure.detail: Any number of 0xFF fill bytes may precede a marker and are not part of any segment: the template skips them with while (ReadUShort(FTell()) == 0xffff) FSkip(1) at line 1542. libjpeg does the same in read_markers and counts what it skips as discarded bytes.
structure.description: Fill bytes are the format's tolerated padding between segments, and they are why a marker search has to skip 0xFF runs.
structure.output_budget: At most a handful of bytes in total across the file; they carry no information and libjpeg reports them through JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA once the count is nonzero.
structure.generation_note: Emit none by default. A generator that wants to exercise libjpeg's extraneous-data warning path may emit a short run of 0xFF bytes before one marker, but never inside entropy-coded data, where 0xFF has the stuffed-byte meaning instead.

structure.subject: restart markers RST0..RST7 inside JPGFILE.scanData
structure.detail: When a DRI segment sets Ri to a nonzero value, the scan must contain a restart marker after every Ri MCUs, cycling 0xFFD0 through 0xFFD7, byte-aligned, with the DC predictors reset to zero at each restart. When Ri is 0 or no DRI is present, no restart marker may appear.
structure.description: Restart markers are the only markers legal inside entropy-coded data, and their spacing is fixed by DRI.Ri.
structure.output_budget: n/a (their bytes are counted inside the scan budget)
structure.generation_note: Keep an MCU counter while emitting the scan; when it reaches Ri, flush to a byte boundary, emit 0xFFD0 + ((counter / Ri) - 1) % 8, reset the DC predictors and continue. Ri itself is a free Tier C count and must not be forced to zero just to avoid implementing this.

structure.subject: SOFx frame header
structure.detail: Exactly one frame header per file. libjpeg aborts with ERREXIT(JERR_SOF_DUPLICATE) -- 'Invalid JPEG file structure: two SOF markers' -- when it sees a second one, and this template would simply parse a second SOFx instance that no decoder accepts.
structure.description: One frame header defines one image; a second one is a structural error rather than a second image.
structure.output_budget: n/a (exactly one, singleton)
structure.generation_note: Emit one SOF only. To vary the frame type across the population, choose among 0xFFC0, 0xFFC1, 0xFFC2 and 0xFFC3 per file rather than emitting several.

structure.subject: Huffman and quantization table slots
structure.detail: At most four DC Huffman tables (htInfo 0x00..0x03), at most four AC Huffman tables (0x10..0x13) and at most four quantization tables (Tq 0..3) may be defined, because those are the slot counts both T.81 and libjpeg use. Several tables may share one DHT or DQT segment; a table may be redefined later, and the last definition before its first use wins.
structure.description: The four-slot limits are what make COMPSOS.DC, COMPSOS.AC, COMPS.compNr and QuanTable.Tq four-value enumerations.
structure.output_budget: A running total of 1024 bytes for all DHT and DQT segments together, inside the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget. Rationale: the four Annex K Huffman tables cost about 420 bytes and two 8-bit quantization tables about 134, so 1024 leaves room for all four Huffman tables plus four quantization tables, including 16-bit ones, without letting the tables crowd out the metadata segments.
structure.generation_note: Emit one DQT segment carrying the tables the frame's components reference, and one DHT segment carrying the DC and AC tables the scans reference; both before the first SOS.

structure.subject: the four APP0 payload flavours
structure.detail: An APP0 segment is exactly one of: JFIF main (identifier 'JFIF\0', lines 1103-1117), JFXX extension (identifier 'JFXX\0', lines 1118-1147), Canon CIFF (two-byte 'II' or 'MM' plus 'HEAPJPGM' at offset 6, lines 1148-1167), or unknown (szSection - 2 opaque bytes, lines 1168-1171). The flavour is decided by the leading bytes and the payloads are incompatible.
structure.description: One APP0 segment cannot be two flavours at once, and each flavour has a completely different internal layout.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a per-segment choice; the bytes are counted in the pre-SOS metadata budget)
structure.generation_note: Pick one flavour per APP0 segment. JFIF main is the one that makes libjpeg set saw_JFIF_marker and therefore influences the colour-space decision; CIFF and JFXX are worth emitting for template-side and metadata-reader diversity.

structure.subject: the three APP1 payload flavours
structure.detail: An APP1 segment is exactly one of: EXIF (identifier 'Exif\0\0', lines 1178-1230), XMP (identifier 'http://ns.adobe.com/xap/1.0/\0', lines 1231-1234), or unknown (szSection - 2 opaque bytes, lines 1235-1238).
structure.description: The two identifiers are mutually exclusive and each selects a different payload structure.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a per-segment choice; the bytes are counted in the pre-SOS metadata budget)
structure.generation_note: Pick one flavour per APP1 segment. Exif 2.2 also fixes the position: the EXIF APP1 should be the first APP1 and should follow the JFIF APP0 when both are present.

structure.subject: the three APP2 payload flavours
structure.detail: An APP2 segment is exactly one of: FlashPix (identifier 'FPXR\0', lines 1245-1249), ICC profile (identifier 'ICC_PROFILE\0', lines 1250-1254), or unknown (lines 1255-1258).
structure.description: The identifiers are mutually exclusive; the ICC flavour additionally requires the block numbering to agree across segments.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a per-segment choice; ICC block bytes are counted in the pre-SOS metadata budget)
structure.generation_note: For an ICC profile, emit block_num = 1..block_total across that many APP2 segments in increasing order; libjpeg-turbo reassembles them in marker order.

structure.subject: the three APP13 payload flavours
structure.detail: An APP13 segment is exactly one of: Photoshop 3.0 image-resource blocks (identifier 'Photoshop 3.0\0', lines 1315-1354), Adobe_CM (identifier 'Adobe_CM\0', lines 1355-1359), or unknown (lines 1360-1363).
structure.description: The two identifiers are mutually exclusive and have different fixed layouts.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a per-segment choice; the bytes are counted in the pre-SOS metadata budget)
structure.generation_note: Pick one flavour per APP13 segment; for the Photoshop flavour emit a chain of IRB blocks whose total size matches szSection.

structure.subject: the frame type: SOF0, SOF1, SOF2, SOF3 or JPGLS (SOF55)
structure.detail: A file carries exactly one frame header and its marker decides the whole coding process: baseline DCT (0xFFC0), extended sequential DCT (0xFFC1), progressive DCT (0xFFC2), lossless sequential (0xFFC3) or JPEG-LS (0xFFF7). The five are mutually exclusive and each changes the rules for precision, sampling factors, scan count, the meaning of Ss/Se/Ah/Al and the entropy coding of the payload.
structure.description: The frame type is the coarsest and most consequential branch in the format.
structure.output_budget: n/a (exactly one frame header, singleton)
structure.generation_note: Choose the frame type per file, then honour its dependency rules: baseline pins Ss=0, Se=63, Ah=0, Al=0 and allows subsampling; progressive forces Hi=Vi=1 and allows several scans; lossless reinterprets Ss as the predictor and needs no AC table; JPEG-LS replaces the Huffman payload with LOCO-I coding entirely and is not implemented by libjpeg.

structure.subject: nested JPEG thumbnails (APP0 JFXX 0x10, APP1 EXIF Compression=6, Casio CasioPreviewThumbnail)
structure.detail: Three places in this template parse a complete JPGFILE inside a metadata segment: the JFXX 0x10 thumbnail bounded by szSection - 8 (lines 1124-1127), the EXIF thumbnail bounded by thumbLength when Compression == 6 (lines 1219-1223), and the Casio preview thumbnail bounded by nComponent (lines 1066-1069). Each is a full JPEG file with its own SOI, tables, scan and EOI.
structure.description: Nested images are real recursive structures in this format, and each one is a second pass through the whole decoder for any reader that displays thumbnails.
structure.output_budget: At most one nested thumbnail per file and at most one level of nesting, with a running total of 2048 bytes for the nested file including its own SOI and EOI. Rationale: a nested thumbnail is a whole second JPEG, so without a bound it multiplies the file size; 2048 bytes is enough for a small valid JPEG (about 100 MCUs of all-zero 4:2:0 scan data plus tables) and keeps the outer image dominant. The bound is on the nested file's total bytes, never on the outer image's dimensions.
structure.generation_note: If a nested thumbnail is wanted, build it as a complete small JPEG first (with the same all-zero scan construction), then embed those bytes and set the enclosing length field (APP0.szSection, or the EXIF ThumbnailLength tag) to cover them exactly. Do not nest a nested thumbnail.

structure.subject: the JFXX 0x11 palette
structure.detail: A palette-indexed JFXX thumbnail carries exactly 256 RGB triplets (768 bytes) followed by one index byte per pixel; the template declares palette[256] at lines 1132-1134 and then pixel[] at line 1135.
structure.description: The palette size is fixed by the format rather than by any field in the file, so it is a cardinality rule and not a count field.
structure.output_budget: Exactly 768 bytes for the palette plus xThumbnail*yThumbnail index bytes, all inside the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget. Rationale: the palette is a fixed cost of choosing this thumbnail encoding; the index count follows the two free dimension bytes and is not capped.
structure.generation_note: Emit 256 triplets (their colour values are free), then one index byte per pixel, then set APP0.szSection = 8 + 768 + xThumbnail*yThumbnail.

structure.subject: every segment length must fit inside the file and inside 65535
structure.detail: szSection is a WORD, so no length-prefixed segment can exceed 65535 bytes including its two length bytes, and a segment must not extend past the end of file -- which this template checks for unknown segments at lines 1406-1408 and warns about. Longer metadata must be split across several segments of the same marker, the way ICC profiles and XMP packets are handled.
structure.description: The 16-bit length field is the format's hard per-segment size limit and the reason multi-block metadata conventions exist.
structure.output_budget: n/a (a per-segment limit imposed by the field width, not a generator budget; the generator's own totals are the two budgets above)
structure.generation_note: When a metadata payload would exceed 65533 bytes, split it: several APP1 segments for XMP, several APP2 blocks with block_num/block_total for an ICC profile, several COM segments for long text.

structure.subject: stray bytes between segments (JPGFILE.garbage)
structure.detail: Bytes that are not 0xFF between segments are tolerated one at a time by this template (line 1621, after the 0xFF test at line 1618) and by libjpeg, which counts them and warns JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA. The template's own history records the fix at lines 18-19: 'Don't fail when garbage bytes are present between JPEG sections'.
structure.description: Inter-segment garbage is tolerated but nearly useless, so it gets a token budget rather than being forbidden outright.
structure.output_budget: At most 16 bytes in total across the whole file. Rationale: the warning path is a couple of lines of decoder code, so a long garbage run would waste output size for almost no coverage; a handful of bytes is enough to reach it.
structure.generation_note: Emit none by default. If emitted, place the bytes between two length-prefixed segments -- never between SOS and EOI, where a non-0xFF byte is valid data but an 0xFF byte must be stuffed.

structure.subject: the EXIF IFD chain inside APP1
structure.detail: TIFF header (align, tagMark 42, offsetFirstIFD) first, then the main image IFD, then optionally the thumbnail IFD at nextIFDoffset, then the out-of-line values and any sub-IFDs (ExifOffset, GPSInfo, InteropOffset, MakerNote) at their own offsets. All offsets are relative to the TIFF header captured at line 1180, not to the file start.
structure.description: The EXIF structure is a linked graph of offsets inside one APP1 segment, so its ordering is about offsets rather than about byte position.
structure.output_budget: Counted inside the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
structure.generation_note: Lay out the TIFF header, then IFD0, then the value area, then IFD1 and the thumbnail; compute every offset as (absolute position - TIFF header position) and write each field in the byte order selected by APP1.align.

structure.subject: APP0 JFIF segment immediately after SOI
structure.detail: JFIF 1.02 clause 3.1 requires the JFIF APP0 segment to be the first segment after SOI in a JFIF-conforming file; JFXX APP0 extension segments follow it. The template does not enforce the position, and neither does libjpeg, but the position is what makes a file JFIF rather than merely JPEG.
structure.description: This is the one ordering rule that comes from a companion specification rather than from T.81 itself.
structure.output_budget: n/a (at most one JFIF main segment, singleton)
structure.generation_note: Emit SOI, then APP0 with 'JFIF\0' when the file is meant to be JFIF, then the rest. Omitting the APP0 is also legal for a plain ISO JPEG and changes libjpeg's colour-space resolution, so both variants are worth generating.

diversity_axes.name: frame width in samples
diversity_axes.why: The image width. It sets the MCU column count, the row stride of every component buffer and the number of pixels the upsampler and colour converter walk per row. This is the field the brief's GIF example destroyed by narrowing it to four values; here it is left completely free and the entropy payload is derived from it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Wide images run the MCU-column and row-buffer loops for many iterations; narrow ones hit the partial-MCU edge case where X is not a multiple of 8*Hmax. libjpeg's jdmaster.c computes MCUs_per_row with a ceil, and jdsample.c's h2v2_upsample handles the last column separately. Widths below one MCU, exactly one MCU and many MCUs take different paths.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Uniform over the whole WORD span the output budget allows, with deliberate weight on the edges: 1, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17 (MCU-boundary neighbours) and large values. Never a fixed set of powers of two.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: The bytes this field costs land in the SOS/scan output_budget (4 bytes per MCU for the all-zero 4:2:0 construction), not in any cap on the field.
diversity_axes.notes: Derive the payload from this field: McuX = ceil(X_image / (8*Hmax)). If one width would exceed the scan budget, lower the sampling factors or the component count for that file -- do not stop emitting large widths across the population.

diversity_axes.name: frame height in lines
diversity_axes.why: The image height. It sets the MCU row count and the number of output scanlines, which drives libjpeg's main-loop iteration count and its output row-buffer recycling.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Tall images run the IDCT, upsample, colour-convert and output pipeline for many rows; short ones hit the partial-MCU bottom edge where Y is not a multiple of 8*Vmax, and a single-MCU-row image exercises the first-row and last-row cases at once. jdmainct.c's context-row buffering differs between one-row, two-row and many-row images.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Uniform over the WORD span the output budget allows, weighted at the edges (1, 7, 8, 9, 15, 16, 17) and including heights that are not multiples of the MCU height.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Same as X_image: the bytes land in the SOS/scan output_budget.
diversity_axes.notes: excluded_values [0] is a format rule (0 means 'unspecified' and needs a DNL this template does not parse), not a narrowing. Derive McuY = ceil(Y_image / (8*Vmax)) from it.

diversity_axes.name: frame type / compression process
diversity_axes.why: The coarsest branch in the format: baseline, extended sequential, progressive or lossless. It changes the scan count, the meaning of Ss/Se/Ah/Al, the sampling-factor rules, the legal precisions and which entropy decoder the file needs.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg dispatches on this at the highest level: SOF0/SOF1 build the single-pass coefficient controller (jdcoefct.c) and the jdhuff.c baseline decoder; SOF2 builds the multi-pass virtual coefficient arrays and the jdphuff.c progressive decoder with its separate first-scan and refinement routines; SOF3 needs jdlhuff.c and the lossless predictor path. Choosing only SOF0 would leave roughly half of libjpeg's decode side untouched.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over all four values across the population, weighted toward 0xFFC0 and 0xFFC2 (the two a mainstream decoder implements fully) but never excluding 0xFFC1 or 0xFFC3.
diversity_axes.notes: Emitting 0xFFC3 against a libjpeg built without C_LOSSLESS_SUPPORTED reaches the JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED path, which is itself a branch worth covering.

diversity_axes.name: sample precision
diversity_axes.why: 8-bit versus 12-bit samples, and 2..16 for the lossless process. It changes the sample width of every buffer, the IDCT scaling and the dequantization arithmetic.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg is compiled for one JSAMPLE width, so a 12-bit file against an 8-bit build reaches ERREXIT1(JERR_BAD_PRECISION) -- a short but distinct path -- while against a 12-bit build it runs the whole pipeline with different sample types. Precision also decides whether 16-bit quantization tables (QuanTable.Pq = 1) mean anything.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 8 in most files and 12 in a minority; for lossless frames span 2..16.
diversity_axes.notes: Never pin this to 8 alone: that silently assumes one decoder build configuration.

diversity_axes.name: number of frame components
diversity_axes.why: How many planes the image has. It decides the colour space, the MCU layout, the blocks per MCU and whether any colour conversion runs at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 1 component: libjpeg sets JCS_GRAYSCALE and skips colour conversion (gray_grayscale_convert, no upsampling when H=V=1). 3 components: JCS_YCbCr, or JCS_RGB with an Adobe transform of 0, giving ycc_rgb_convert plus the chroma upsamplers. 4 components: JCS_CMYK or JCS_YCCK, giving ycck_cmyk_convert and the four-plane MCU layout. 2 components: reaches the setup path and then JERR_BAD_J_COLORSPACE. Four genuinely different back halves of the decoder.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over 1, 3 and 4 as the main cases (the three that decode fully) and emit 2 occasionally; never more than 4.
diversity_axes.notes: valid_values is [1,2,3,4] with completeness partial and the reason recorded in the entry: counts of 5 and above abort in default_jpeg_colorspace before any pixel work.

diversity_axes.name: frame component identifiers
diversity_axes.why: The identifier each component carries. Free apart from distinctness, and the scan header mirrors it -- so this is a field whose freedom propagates rather than one that is merely unconstrained.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg matches scan component ids against these by value, and its colour-space guess consults them too (ids 1,2,3 in order suggest YCbCr when no JFIF or Adobe segment says otherwise). Unusual ids therefore reach the id-based branch of default_jpeg_colorspace that a canonical file never touches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Mostly the conventional 1..N, but a minority of files should use shifted or descending ids (e.g. 5,6,7 or 3,2,1) to reach the id-based colour-space branch.
diversity_axes.notes: The scan header's COMPSOS.compId is derived from this field; never narrow these ids to make a fixed scan header work.

diversity_axes.name: horizontal sampling factors
diversity_axes.why: Hi per component. Together with Vert it decides the MCU width, the blocks per MCU, the subsampling ratio and which upsampler libjpeg instantiates.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: All factors 1: no upsampling at all (jdsample.c's noop_upsample). 2:1 horizontal: h2v1_upsample. 2:2: h2v2_upsample, plus jdmaster.c's merged-upsample optimisation when the colour converter and the sampling ratio allow it. 3:1, 4:1, 2:3 and other ratios: the generic int_upsample path. Each is a separate function, so this pair of fields selects a large slice of the decoder's output side.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit the canonical 4:2:0 (Y=2, Cb=Cr=1) and 4:4:4 (all 1) often, but rotate through every legal factor including 3 and 4, and through asymmetric combinations where the luma and chroma factors differ.
diversity_axes.notes: Hmax = max(Horz) feeds McuX = ceil(X_image / (8*Hmax)) in the payload's generation_strategy: derive the payload from these factors, never cap them to suit a precomputed scan.

diversity_axes.name: vertical sampling factors
diversity_axes.why: Vi per component. The vertical half of the subsampling ratio, and the factor that decides whether libjpeg can use its merged two-pass upsampler.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: V=1 with H=2 gives h2v1_upsample (one output row per input row); V=2 gives h2v2_upsample and makes jdmaster.c consider using_merged_upsample, which fuses upsampling with colour conversion -- a substantially different output path. V=3 or 4 forces the generic int_upsample row replication. Vertical factors also change the MCU height and therefore the number of MCU rows for a given image height.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate through 1..4 independently of Horz so that both the h2v1/h2v2 fast paths and the generic path appear in the population.
diversity_axes.notes: Vmax = max(Vert) feeds McuY = ceil(Y_image / (8*Vmax)); blocks per MCU = sum(Hi*Vi).

diversity_axes.name: components per scan
diversity_axes.why: Ns: how many components one scan carries. In a progressive file it is what makes single-component scans possible, and in any file it fixes the blocks-per-MCU of that scan.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg's jdmaster.c chooses the MCU layout from comps_in_scan, and jdcoefct.c/jdphuff.c pick different MCU-decoding routines for a single-component scan than for a multi-component interleaved scan; Ns = 1 also enables the single-component fast paths in the upsampler.
diversity_axes.how_varied: For baseline files Ns must equal SOFx.nr_comp; for progressive files vary it -- single-component scans, all-component scans and partial subsets.

diversity_axes.name: scan component references
diversity_axes.why: Cs: the frame-component id each scan slot refers to. It is derived, not free, and the derivation is the instruction here: mirror SOFx.COMPS.compId.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg searches the frame component list for each Cs and aborts with JERR_BAD_COMPONENT_ID before any entropy decoding when one is missing. The order of ids within a scan also decides the block order inside an MCU, which changes the entropy payload's shape.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Not varied directly: copy the ids written into the frame header, in the order the scan needs them.
diversity_axes.notes: This axis exists to state the pairing: COMPS.compId is the free field and this one is computed from it. A rewrite step that pins either one has inverted the dependency.

diversity_axes.name: Huffman table selectors
diversity_axes.why: Tdc and Tda per scan component: which of the four DC and four AC table slots the scan uses.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg resolves dc_huff_tbl_ptrs[td] and ac_huff_tbl_ptrs[ta] when it starts the entropy pass; an empty slot aborts with JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE. Different table selections mean different derived decode tables, hence different code lengths and different bit consumption per MCU -- the same coefficients produce different bytes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Mostly 0 (the canonical single-table case), but a minority of files should define two or four tables and assign them per component so the multi-table lookup paths run.
diversity_axes.notes: Every selector used must have a matching DHT earlier in the file.

diversity_axes.name: spectral selection window
diversity_axes.why: Ss and Se: which DCT coefficients a progressive scan carries. In a baseline scan a dependency pins them to 0 and 63; in a progressive scan they are the scan's whole purpose.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg's jdphuff.c selects decode_mcu_DC_first (Ss = Se = 0), decode_mcu_AC_first (Ss > 0 with Ah = 0) or the refinement variants from these two bytes, and jdcoefct.c derives its coefficient access pattern from them. DC-only, AC-only, narrow-window and wide-window scans are four different decoder loops.
diversity_axes.how_varied: For progressive files emit the canonical splits (DC scan Ss=Se=0; one AC scan Ss=1,Se=63; several AC scans such as 1..5 then 6..63; luma and chrominance separated) plus odd windows like Ss=63,Se=63.
diversity_axes.notes: Baseline files must use Ss=0 and Se=63 -- that is a dependency, not a narrowing of this axis.

diversity_axes.name: successive approximation
diversity_axes.why: Ah and Al: the bit-plane window of a progressive scan. Ah = 0 means a first scan; Ah > 0 means a refinement scan.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Ah > 0 switches libjpeg to decode_mcu_DC_refine and decode_mcu_AC_refine in jdphuff.c, which read one correction bit per coefficient and use a different EOB-run encoding. Al decides how many low bits are withheld and therefore the magnitude arithmetic. These are large, separate blocks of decoder code that a first-scan-only population never reaches.
diversity_axes.how_varied: For progressive files emit first scans (Ah = 0, with Al varying) and refinement scans (Ah > 0, Al = Ah - 1) so both families run; keep both inside 0..13.
diversity_axes.notes: Baseline files must use Ah = 0 and Al = 0 by dependency.

diversity_axes.name: restart interval
diversity_axes.why: The MCU count between restart markers. A free Tier C count, and the switch that turns libjpeg's whole restart subsystem on or off.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Ri = 0: the entropy decoder never calls process_restart. Ri > 0: jdhuff.c's process_restart runs at every interval -- it discards buffered bits, realigns to a byte boundary, reads and validates the RSTn marker, resets the DC predictors and the EOB run counter, and jdcoefct.c re-primes its MCU buffer. That is a substantial amount of code reachable only when this field is nonzero.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit no DRI segment (or Ri = 0) for part of the population and nonzero Ri for the rest, spanning small intervals (1, 2, 3), intervals that divide the MCU count exactly, and intervals that do not (which exercise the partial final restart group).
diversity_axes.notes: The payload must insert RSTn markers every Ri MCUs. Derive the payload from Ri; never force Ri to 0 to avoid implementing restarts.

diversity_axes.name: entropy-coded payload
diversity_axes.why: The compressed image data itself. Its framing is Tier A and its contents are free -- the pairing that buys depth and diversity at once.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: This is where nearly all of a JPEG decoder's execution lives: Huffman symbol decoding, DC difference accumulation, AC run decoding, dequantization, the IDCT including its 'AC terms all zero' fast path, upsampling, colour conversion and the output row loop. Every coefficient pattern takes a slightly different route through it.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Build the all-zero floor from the entry's generation_strategy, then vary the coefficients freely: nonzero DC categories, sparse nonzero AC coefficients, runs long enough to need ZRL, large magnitudes, and per-file variation in which blocks carry energy. Always re-derive the MCU count from the geometry and re-stuff every 0xFF.
diversity_axes.notes: content_is_free is true: the coefficients inside a well-formed scan are unconstrained. What must not vary is the framing -- valid Huffman codes, the right MCU count, byte stuffing and correct restart placement.

diversity_axes.name: table class and destination
diversity_axes.why: Tc and Th: whether a table is DC or AC and which of the four slots it fills. It decides which symbol vocabulary is legal and which selector may reference the table.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg files the table under dc_huff_tbl_ptrs[th] or ac_huff_tbl_ptrs[th] and validates the symbol vocabulary by class in jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl; a scan that selects a slot never filled aborts with JERR_NO_HUFF_TABLE. Filling all eight slots produces a different set of lookups from filling two.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit at least one DC and one AC table in every file (slot 0 of each); in a minority of files fill slots 1..3 as well and reference them from the scan header.
diversity_axes.notes: valid_values are the eight combinations 0x00..0x03 and 0x10..0x13; the upper three bits of the byte must be zero.

diversity_axes.name: code-length counts
diversity_axes.why: L1..L16: the shape of the Huffman code. Free counts, and the source of table-shape diversity in the population.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg's jpeg_make_d_derived_tbl builds its look-ahead tables from these counts: a different distribution changes the derived table's size, the number of slow-path get_more_bits calls during decoding and the code lengths the entropy decoder walks. A flat table and the Annex K table take measurably different routes through the same function.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit the Annex K tables verbatim in most files (the safest correct construction) and hand-built tables -- shorter, longer, deliberately incomplete -- in a minority, always satisfying sum <= 256 and the Kraft inequality.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the DHT/DQT budget (1024 bytes) inside the pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: The symbol array's extent is derived from these counts (local sumLen), so HTV is sized from this field rather than the other way round.

diversity_axes.name: Huffman symbol values
diversity_axes.why: The symbols assigned to each code, in increasing code order. Their vocabulary is fixed by the table class, but which symbols appear and how many of each is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The symbol values decide what a decoded code means: DC categories 0..11, or AC run/size pairs plus EOB and ZRL. A table that omits a symbol forces the payload to avoid it; a table that includes 0xF0 lets the payload exercise libjpeg's 16-zero run handling.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Follow the Annex K symbol order in most files; in others permute or subset the symbols, always keeping EOB for AC tables and keeping the multiset consistent with Huffmann_Table.length.
diversity_axes.notes: The legal vocabulary is a pattern rather than a list, which is why the entry uses pattern_constraint with the DC and AC rules spelled out.

diversity_axes.name: quantization values
diversity_axes.why: The 64 dequantization divisors of a table. Free numbers, and the direct control over every reconstructed pixel value.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg multiplies each decoded coefficient by its table entry during dequantization and then runs jpeg_idct_islow. A block whose AC coefficients all dequantize to zero takes the IDCT's explicit 'AC terms all zero' fast path, which fills the block from the DC value alone; any nonzero AC term takes the full 8x8 path. Table values therefore switch branches of the IDCT, with large values pushing coefficients to zero and small ones keeping them nonzero.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the full element range: all-ones tables, the Annex K suggested tables scaled by various quality factors, tables containing zeros, tables with very large values, and asymmetric tables whose DC element differs sharply from their AC elements.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the DHT/DQT budget: 67 bytes per 8-bit table, 131 per 16-bit table.
diversity_axes.notes: Zero elements are legal: decoding multiplies by the table, so a zero forces that coefficient to zero rather than dividing by it.

diversity_axes.name: quantization element width and table slot
diversity_axes.why: Pq selects 8-bit or 16-bit table elements and Tq selects which of the four slots the table fills; both change the segment layout and the decoder's dequantization setup.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg reads a Pq=1 table into 16-bit entries and scales it for the output precision, a different branch of get_dqt and of the IDCT initialiser. Tq above 3 aborts with JERR_DQT_INDEX. Filling several slots and pointing different components at them changes which table each component's IDCT uses.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Mostly Pq=0 with Tq=0 (and Tq=1 for chroma in a three-component file); emit Pq=1 and the higher slots in a minority of files.
diversity_axes.notes: A 16-bit table doubles the DQT segment length, which DQT.szSection must reflect.

diversity_axes.name: per-component quantization table selection
diversity_axes.why: Tqi per component: which quantization table each plane uses. Sharing one table across all components versus giving luma and chroma separate tables changes the dequantized coefficients of every block.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg resolves quant_tbl_ptrs[tq] per component at IDCT setup and aborts with JERR_NO_QUANT_TABLE when a slot is empty. Different tables per component also change which coefficients land on zero, and therefore which IDCT fast path each component takes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Mostly 0 for every component (the single-table case) or 0 for luma and 1 for chroma; rotate through the higher slots in a minority of files.
diversity_axes.notes: Every slot used must be filled by a DQT earlier in the file.

diversity_axes.name: JFIF thumbnail dimensions and density words
diversity_axes.why: The JFIF thumbnail's width and height, and the two density words. All four are free metadata numbers, and the thumbnail dimensions size a real byte array (3*x*y RGB triplets) that the parser derives from them.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg reads the thumbnail dimensions into cinfo->thumb_width/thumb_height and cross-checks them against the remaining APP0 length, warning when they disagree; the density unit and the two density words are stored and reported to the caller. A thumbnail present versus absent, and a matching versus a mismatching size, are distinct branches of get_app0.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit no thumbnail (both bytes 0) in most files; when present, span small and large dimensions and both the matching and mismatching size cases. For the density words, span the WORD range with both zero excluded and units varied over 0, 1 and 2.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: The thumbnail's 3*x*y bytes count against the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget, so a file that wants a large thumbnail emits fewer other metadata segments. The dimensions themselves are never capped to achieve that.
diversity_axes.notes: Derive the thumbnail bytes and APP0.szSection from these two free dimensions; never pick dimensions that make a precomputed thumbnail fit.

diversity_axes.name: JFIF version and density units
diversity_axes.why: The JFIF version pair and the density-unit selector: three small enumerations that a JFIF-aware reader interprets and that libjpeg stores.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg's get_app0 copies the major and minor version and the density unit into the decompress struct without validating them, so these are branches in the reader-facing API rather than in the decode; a JFIF 2.00 declaration also changes the segment layout, which is worth covering.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 1.02 (major 1, minor 2) most of the time and rotate through major 1 with minor 0 and 1, major 2, and all three density units.

diversity_axes.name: JFXX thumbnail encoding
diversity_axes.why: Which of the three JFXX thumbnail encodings an APP0 extension segment carries: a nested JPEG, a palette-indexed image or RGB triplets.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each code selects a completely different payload layout -- a recursive JPGFILE parse for 0x10, a fixed 256-entry palette plus indices for 0x11, and raw triplets for 0x13 -- and an unrecognised code reaches the template's default branch. For a decoder that displays JFXX thumbnails these are three separate code paths.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over 0x10, 0x11 and 0x13; emit an unrecognised code occasionally to reach the unknown-payload branch.
diversity_axes.notes: 0x10 makes the payload a whole nested JPEG, so its bytes count against the nested thumbnail budget in the structure section.

diversity_axes.name: metadata byte order selectors
diversity_axes.why: The two byte-order words in the file: Canon CIFF's 'II'/'MM' in APP0 and the TIFF/EXIF 'II'/'MM' in APP1. Each one flips the endianness of every field that follows it inside its own block.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The template calls LittleEndian() or leaves BigEndian() on the strength of one character (lines 1156 and 1182), so the two values produce two different parses of the same bytes. Any EXIF or CIFF reader has the same fork, and little-endian EXIF is extremely common in real files -- omitting it would leave half of that code untested.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit 'MM' and 'II' roughly equally across the population, and mix them: a big-endian JPEG carrying little-endian EXIF is the common real-world case.
diversity_axes.notes: The surrounding JPEG markers and lengths stay big-endian whichever value is chosen.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF thumbnail payload
diversity_axes.why: The bytes of an embedded EXIF thumbnail. Free when the Compression tag says 'uncompressed' and a complete nested JPEG when it says 6.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: For a reader that decodes thumbnails this is a second full JPEG decode; for libjpeg it is skipped entirely. The interesting variation is presence versus absence, nested-JPEG versus raw strip, and the size the ThumbnailLength tag claims.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit no thumbnail IFD in most files; when present, alternate between a nested JPEG (Compression = 6) and a raw strip, and vary the claimed length.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted against the 2048-byte nested-thumbnail budget in the structure section when the thumbnail is a nested JPEG.
diversity_axes.notes: When Compression = 6 the payload must be a whole JPEG file; that conditional requirement is a dependency, not a cap on this field.

diversity_axes.name: ICC profile block numbering
diversity_axes.why: The one-based block index and the shared block total for a multi-block ICC profile, plus the FlashPix version byte. Free counts whose only rule is that they agree across the file's APP2 segments.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg-turbo's jpeg_read_icc_profile() walks the marker list, checks that every block carries the ICC_PROFILE prefix, that block_total agrees and that block_num covers 1..block_total exactly once; only then does it concatenate and validate the 128-byte profile header. A single-block and a many-block profile take different routes through that reassembly loop.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit a single-block profile (1/1) often and multi-block profiles with block_total from 2 upward occasionally; vary the FlashPix version byte freely.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: All ICC block bytes count against the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: APP2.szSection is a derived length and appears here only so the pairing is explicit: the profile is split to suit the free counts, never the reverse.

diversity_axes.name: Ducky entry chain
diversity_axes.why: The Ducky entry tags and the free value, count and text they carry. A small chain format inside one APP12 segment.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each tag selects a different entry layout (a uint32 quality value, or a count plus text), and DK_End terminates the chain, so the tag value and the chain length are both real branches for any reader that parses Ducky data. libjpeg skips the segment by length.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over DK_Quality, DK_Comment and DK_Copyright entries in varying numbers and orderings, always ending the chain with DK_End; vary the free text length widely.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: APP12.len is derived from the entry content, so the text length is the free quantity and the length field is computed from it. The free value, count and text fields are covered by the APP12.count axis.

diversity_axes.name: Photoshop image-resource chain
diversity_axes.why: The IRB block signature, the resource id, the name length and the data size: a chain of variable-length blocks inside one APP13 segment, plus the Adobe_CM alternative flavour.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each resource id names a different payload sub-format (IPTC records, an embedded thumbnail, an ICC profile, an XMP packet), and the block loop's alignment padding gives two more branches. libjpeg skips APP13 by length, so this is metadata-reader coverage rather than decode coverage -- but the template parses it in full and the blocks are a real chain format.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit '8BIM' blocks with a rotating selection of resource ids, with and without names, with odd and even data sizes (to reach both padding branches), and emit the 'PHUT'/'DCSR'/'AgHg' signatures and the Adobe_CM flavour occasionally.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: APP13.size is derived from the data length; the data bytes themselves are free and are covered, with the name and padding fields, by the APP13.data axis.

diversity_axes.name: Adobe colour transform
diversity_axes.why: The Adobe APP14 transform code, plus the two flag words that accompany it. The code is the only one of the three that a decoder acts on.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg stores the code as cinfo->Adobe_transform and uses it in default_jpeg_colorspace: transform 0 with three components gives JCS_RGB (rgb_rgb_convert, effectively a copy), 1 gives JCS_YCbCr (ycc_rgb_convert), and with four components 0 gives JCS_CMYK while 1 or 2 give JCS_YCCK (ycck_cmyk_convert). Those are three different colour-conversion routines, so this one byte selects a large slice of jdcolor.c.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over 0, 1 and 2, pairing 0 and 1 with three-component frames and 0, 1 and 2 with four-component frames; vary the two flag words freely since libjpeg discards them.
diversity_axes.notes: Emitting the APP14 segment at all sets cinfo->saw_Adobe_marker, which by itself changes the colour-space resolution, so presence versus absence is part of this axis.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF tag vocabulary
diversity_axes.why: Which EXIF, GPS or Casio tag a directory entry carries, and the free or enumerated value slots that go with it. The tag decides the entry's interpretation, including whether its value is a number, a string or a pointer.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The template switches on the tag in four places: Make and Model are copied into buffers that later gate the Casio MakerNote branch; ExifOffset, GPSInfo, InteropOffset, MakerNote and CasioPreviewThumbnail are followed as nested structures; the thumbnail geometry tags are collected to locate the embedded image; and eight tags get an inline enum interpretation (ExposureProgram, MeteringMode, LightSource, Flash, ExposureMode, WhiteBalance, SceneCaptureType, SubjectDistanceRange). Each is a distinct branch. libjpeg parses none of it, so this axis is about metadata-reader and template coverage.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Include the pointer tags (ExifOffset, GPSInfo, InteropOffset) and the thumbnail tags (Compression, ThumbnailOffset, ThumbnailLength) in some files so the nested branches run; rotate the eight enum-interpreted tags through all their legal values; vary the plain value slots freely.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: All EXIF bytes count against the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: The Flash tag's six bitfields are enumerated per bit, so rotating through all legal values there means spanning the bit combinations rather than picking one.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF value types and counts
diversity_axes.why: The data-type code of an entry and the element count that goes with it: together they decide the value's byte length, whether the value is inline or pointed at, and how much padding follows.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Twelve data types give twelve value-parsing branches in the template (byte, ASCII, short, long, rational, signed byte, undefined, signed short, signed long, signed rational, float, double), and the length <= 4 test splits every one of them into an inline and a pointed-at case. That is the largest branch fan-out in the EXIF structure.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate over all twelve data types and, for each, choose element counts on both sides of the four-byte inline boundary (1, 2, 4, 5, 16, 100 ...) so the inline, padded and offset cases all appear.
diversity_axes.notes: nComponent stays a free count and has its own axis: the length relation is a dependency and the total EXIF bytes are bounded by the metadata budget, not by this field.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF and CIFF directory sizes
diversity_axes.why: The number of directory entries in the EXIF and CIFF directories, plus the Casio MakerNote header bytes. These are the repeat counts that decide how much metadata a file carries.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The template allocates and loops over exactly nDirEntry records in both IFD and CDIR, so the count drives the loop trip count and the offset arithmetic that follows. A directory with one entry and one with fifty take the same code but lay the value area out differently. libjpeg parses none of it.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span small (0, 1, 2) and large entry counts, and vary the CIFF directory count independently of the EXIF one.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget; a large directory simply crowds out other metadata segments.
diversity_axes.notes: Neither count is capped to keep files small: the metadata budget is the only size control, exactly as the brief requires.

diversity_axes.name: CIFF record layout selectors
diversity_axes.why: The CIFF storage selector, data type and tag id: three small fields that between them decide where a record's value lives and how it is interpreted.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: storage_method 0 sends the parser to the heap at oData for sData bytes, 1 reads the value inline; data_type then selects byte, ASCII, word, dword or nested-directory interpretation, with the shifts (sData>>1, sData>>2) giving further branches; id_code selects the two records the template understands specially (kTC_ImageFormat inline, kTC_ImageSpec as a DC_IMAGESPEC record). That is a real branch fan-out for any CIFF reader.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit both storage methods, all seven data types and the recognised tag ids, plus unrecognised ids so the default eight-byte branch runs.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: The two reserved storage_method values (2 and 3) are legal to emit and reach the inline branch, since the template only tests for kStg_InHeapSpace. The free inline value words (fileFormat, targetCompressionRatio) have their own axis.

diversity_axes.name: CIFF image-spec record
diversity_axes.why: The seven words of the CIFF kTC_ImageSpec heap record: declared width and height, pixel aspect ratio, rotation angle, component and colour bit depths, and the colour/monochrome flag.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: These are camera-private metadata: no JPEG decoder reads them, and this template only stores them. They are recorded as an axis because two of them are dimensions and three are bit depths -- exactly the fields a size-conscious author would be tempted to pin -- and pinning them would remove diversity without reaching a single new line of decoder code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the WORD/DWORD ranges and include zero, negative (for the signed rotation angle) and float edge patterns (0.0, NaN, infinity) freely.
diversity_axes.notes: The record's 28-byte extent is fixed by its type, so sData must be at least 28 when this record is present; the values inside it are free.

diversity_axes.name: comment text
diversity_axes.why: The COM segment's text: free bytes whose length is the only thing that reaches back into the segment header.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg skips COM segments by length, so the content changes nothing in the decode; what it does change is the file's byte profile and the segment-length arithmetic. The template prints the text after replacing embedded NULs (lines 1495-1502), which is a display path worth reaching with varied content.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Vary the length from empty (szSection = 2) to the segment maximum, and the content freely including NUL bytes, 0xFF bytes and non-ASCII.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget; several COM segments may be emitted to carry more text than one segment allows.
diversity_axes.notes: szSection is derived from the chosen text length -- derive the length from the content, never pick a short comment to keep the file small.

diversity_axes.name: unrecognised marker vocabulary
diversity_axes.why: The marker code of a segment this template does not model, and therefore which of the format's reserved or unsupported markers a file may carry.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg handles unrecognised markers in read_markers: a length-prefixed unknown marker is skipped, while the unsupported frame types it does recognise (SOF5..SOF7, SOF9..SOF11, SOF13..SOF15) abort with JERR_SOF_UNSUPPORTED, as do the arithmetic-coding markers. Those are distinct error paths, and the template's own default branch splits again on whether the byte is 0xFF (a length-prefixed UNKNOWN segment) or not (a single garbage byte).
diversity_axes.how_varied: Rotate through the length-prefixed markers the template does not parse (M_APP3 to M_APP11, M_APP15, M_JPG 0xFFC8, M_DAC 0xFFCC, M_EXP 0xFFDF, M_SOF5 to M_SOF7, M_SOF9 to M_SOF11, M_SOF13 to M_SOF15) and the standalone ones (TEM 0xFF01, and RST0..RST7 outside scan data), each with a consistent szSection.
diversity_axes.notes: The lookahead at line 1618 (ReadUByte == 0xff) decides UNKNOWN versus garbage; both branches are worth reaching.

diversity_axes.name: tolerated stray and trailing bytes
diversity_axes.why: Stray bytes between segments, trailing bytes after EOI, and the truncated-scan fallback when no EOI is found: three tolerated byte runs whose values are unchecked.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg counts extraneous bytes before a marker and warns JWRN_EXTRANEOUS_DATA, then continues; it ignores everything after EOI; and a missing EOI produces JWRN_HIT_MARKER with the remaining MCUs filled grey. Each is a short but real warning path, and none is worth more than a handful of bytes.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Emit none in most files; occasionally a few stray bytes between two segments and a short trailing run after EOI. Never omit EOI: unterminatedScanData describes a broken file and produces a shallower parse, not a deeper one.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: At most 16 bytes of inter-segment garbage (structure section); trailing bytes after EOI are unbounded but pointless, so keep them small.
diversity_axes.notes: unterminatedScanData is covered here only to record that a generator must not aim for it.

diversity_axes.name: hierarchical parent geometry
diversity_axes.why: The parent image's width and height in a T.81 annex E hierarchical file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg does not implement hierarchical JPEG and refuses the DHP marker, so these fields reach an error path rather than a decode; for a decoder that does implement annex E they are the parent geometry the differential levels refine, and they drive the same buffer-sizing and row-loop code as SOFx.X_image and Y_image.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the WORD range with the same edge weighting as the frame dimensions (1, 7, 8, 9, 16 and large values).
diversity_axes.notes: Hierarchical files are a minority case: emit them occasionally for the marker-level error path, not as the population's main shape.

diversity_axes.name: hierarchical parent parameters
diversity_axes.why: The parent sample precision, component count and per-component sampling factors in a DHP segment.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: For an annex E decoder these mirror the SOF fields and select the same sample-width, colour-space and upsampling paths; for libjpeg they are unreachable because the marker itself is refused. They are enumerated so that a file targeting an annex E decoder emits legal values rather than arbitrary ones.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Precision mostly 8 with occasional 12 and the rest of 2..16; component counts 1, 3 and 4; sampling factors rotated through 1..4 as for SOFx.
diversity_axes.notes: DHP.Tq is covered by the COMPS.compNr axis, since both are quantization-table selectors.

diversity_axes.name: JPEG-LS frame geometry
diversity_axes.why: The width and height of a JPEG-LS (SOF-55) frame. A height of zero is legal here, unlike SOFx.Y_image, so this pair carries no excluded value at all.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A T.87 decoder such as CharLS sizes its line buffers and its context-modelling loop from these two words; a height of zero makes it decode until the data runs out, which is a distinct path from the sized case. libjpeg refuses the marker outright.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the WORD range including 0 for Y_numlines (legal in JPEG-LS) and the usual edge values for both.
diversity_axes.notes: Do not carry the SOFx.Y_image excluded_values [0] rule over to this field: T.87 permits Y = 0.

diversity_axes.name: JPEG-LS frame parameters
diversity_axes.why: The JPEG-LS sample precision, component count, component id and interleave byte.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: CharLS branches on the precision to choose its sample width and on the component count and interleave mode to choose its line loop (single-component, line-interleaved or sample-interleaved), so these four small fields select most of a JPEG-LS decoder's configuration space.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Precision mostly 8 with the rest of 2..16 rotated in; component counts 1, 3 and 4; interleave modes 0..3 where the byte is read as ILV.
diversity_axes.notes: JPGLS.Tq is Tier A fixed 0 on the strength of the template's own comment and is therefore not an axis; JPGLS.C_compID is covered by the COMPS.compId axis.

diversity_axes.name: ICC profile payload
diversity_axes.why: The profile fragment carried by an APP2 ICC block. Its 128-byte header and tag table are Tier A framing; everything inside the tags is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg-turbo's jpeg_read_icc_profile() validates the reassembled header before any tag is walked, so a well-formed header is what opens the ICC path at all: profile size, device class, colour space, PCS, the 'acsp' signature and the tag table's offsets and sizes. Inside the tags -- the description string, the tone-reproduction curves, the chromaticity and white-point data -- nothing is checked, so those bytes are pure diversity. A malformed header drops the profile silently and skips all of that code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Build one header shape per file and vary its free content: device class (mntr, scnr, prtr), colour space (RGB, GRAY, CMYK), tag count from 1 upward, tag data of different lengths, and the MD5 and date fields. Vary the fragment size so that single-block and multi-block profiles both appear.
diversity_axes.notes: Derive the fragment sizes from the free block counts and the profile length, then patch the header's size field; never shorten the profile to fit a fixed block count.

diversity_axes.name: Ducky entry values and text
diversity_axes.why: The free uint32 value of a DK_Quality entry, the byte count that precedes a comment or copyright entry, and the comment text itself.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg skips APP12 entirely, so these fields reach no decoder branch; they are recorded as an axis because they are exactly the kind of free metadata numbers a size-conscious author would pin, and pinning them would make every Ducky block in the population identical.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the uint32 range for the value and count fields and vary the text length from 0 up to what the metadata budget allows.
diversity_axes.notes: APP12.len is computed from the chosen text length; the text is free and the length follows it.

diversity_axes.name: Photoshop IRB block contents
diversity_axes.why: The resource data bytes, the optional name and its length, the two alignment padding bytes and the Adobe_CM type byte: the free interior of each image-resource block.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: libjpeg skips APP13 by length, so none of these bytes reach a decoder branch. They are the largest free byte run in the metadata and the cheapest source of file-to-file difference; the only rules that apply are the parity paddings and the size field, both of which are dependencies.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Vary the data length widely (including 0, which omits the data field entirely), emit names of odd and even lengths to reach both padding branches, and vary the data bytes freely.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: APP13.size is derived from the chosen data length.

diversity_axes.name: Adobe APP14 flag words
diversity_axes.why: The two Adobe flag words. Adobe TN 5116 gives individual bits meanings, but libjpeg reads both words and discards them, keeping only the version and the transform code.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: No decoder branch depends on these 32 bits, so they are pure entropy: leaving them free adds file-to-file difference at zero cost in depth. This is the documented close call of the extraction -- flag words normally look like Tier B, and the tier test (what does a decoder do with a wrong value?) answers 'nothing at all', which puts them in Tier C.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span both words freely, including the bits Adobe defines and all-zero, since nothing validates them.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF inline value slots
diversity_axes.why: The inline value slots of an EXIF entry -- the uShort and uLong words, the reserved high bits of the Flash tag, and the padding that fills an inline value out to four bytes.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: These are the generic value words every EXIF tag uses; the template interprets them only for a handful of tags (Compression into a nested-JPEG decision, the offset tags into seeks) and libjpeg reads none of them. Free values here are what make two EXIF blocks differ.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Vary the value words freely across their full width; for the offset-bearing tags compute the offset from the layout instead of choosing it freely. Vary the reserved Flash bits and the padding bytes freely too.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: Where a tag does define a legal set (Compression = 1 or 6), the dependency section narrows the slot for that tag only -- a format rule, not a cap on the field.

diversity_axes.name: EXIF element counts
diversity_axes.why: The number of value elements in an EXIF entry. It multiplies the data-type width to give the value's byte length and sizes every value array the template reads.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: No decoder reads it, but it is a count that feeds an allocation and a loop, which is precisely the class of field the brief says must stay free. Capping it would give every EXIF block the same shape for no depth at all.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span small counts (1, 2, 4) that keep the value inline and large counts (5, 16, 100, 1000) that force the offsetData path, always keeping the value inside the segment.
diversity_axes.diversity_budget: Counted in the 4096-byte pre-SOS metadata budget.
diversity_axes.notes: The length relation (dataFormatLength[dataFormat] * nComponent, inline when <= 4) is a dependency; the count itself is never capped.

diversity_axes.name: CIFF inline record values
diversity_axes.why: The CIFF kTC_ImageFormat record's two inline words: a file-format uint32 and a compression ratio float.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Camera-private metadata that no JPEG decoder inspects and this template only stores. They are recorded as an axis because a format word and a float both invite pinning, and pinning them would remove diversity without reaching any code.
diversity_axes.how_varied: Span the uint32 range and the float bit patterns freely, including 0.0, negative, very large, NaN and infinity.
